Part 1 · How to Read This Handbook

From the big picture to daily operations, then into the API, data and operations.

What the documentation inventory found

The repository already holds a considerable amount of documentation, but as of this inventory there is no single, continuously readable HTML handbook that covers all 11 applications and services. The existing Traditional Chinese role guides are detailed, with a main update date of 2025-10-26; the flow-level documents are newer but are scattered across 17 Markdown files and several verification reports. This handbook brings operations, integration, development and maintenance together into one reading path.

Existing document Purpose Limitations when reading
Shop Owner guideand the Customer, Chef, Service Crew and Cashier guides Role training, screens and daily operations Older entry points, permissions, payment and offline descriptions must be checked against the current code.
System architecture diagram Relationships between apps, Workers, packages and bindings Describes structure only; it cannot replace step-by-step operation.
Master flow diagramand 17 flow documents Role and cross-app flows, errors, race conditions Some passages still keep historical behavior; where they conflict, this handbook follows the current source code.
CLAUDE.md and runbooks Development conventions, D1 migrations, incident handling Engineering reference, not a complete end-user training manual.
2026-10-04 flow verification Most recent regression evidence, limitations and gaps Dated local / production snapshots; passing tests does not mean an external provider is connected.

Choose a reading path by your role

  • First time with the system:Part 1 → 2 → 3 → 4. Learn the big picture, identity and orders first, then read the apps you use.
  • Shop Owner:Part 2 → 3 → 6 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10 → 16 → 19.
  • Customers and customer support:Part 3 → 4 → 5 → 19, paying particular attention to guest order credentials and payment status.
  • Kitchen, Service Crew, Cashier:Part 4 → 7 → 8 → 9 → 10. The three stations handle different stages of the same order.
  • Platform administrators:Part 11 → 12 → 13 → 16 → 18 → 20.
  • Development and integration:Part 2 → 3 → 4 → 13 → 14 → 15 → 17 → 18 → appendices.

Three kinds of evidence in this handbook

  • Current source code:This verification read the repository code, routers, schemas and configuration directly; it refers to the behavior of the local version.
  • Configuration defaults:Flags and declarations in wrangler.toml. A real deployment may override them; this verification did not sign in to Cloudflare again to query every production setting.
  • Dated verification:Cites existing investigations and keeps their environment and date. A past success, empty data or missing credentials must not be taken as the permanent production state.

This is a handbook for "understanding and operating the system", not a declaration that every feature is live in production. Features without a provider, flag, production data or hardware acceptance are listed together with their prerequisites for enabling.

Reading and carrying the handbook

This file ships its own CSS and search script, with no external fonts, CDN or network dependency. Double-click the HTML to read it; the top right lets you print or save as PDF. Chapter search lists related chapters; to find exact text within a page, use your browser's Ctrl/Cmd + F. If the HTML is forwarded on its own, the main text stays readable; the source links need the repository's relative directory structure to be preserved.

Part 2 · System Overview and App Responsibilities

Five front ends, five Cloudflare Workers, plus one in-store print agent.

Product model

MakanMasak is a multi-restaurant platform for food and service management. Customers enter from a table / seat / shop QR code, the discovery page or a market; the Shop Owner maintains the menu and store operations; the kitchen prepares; Service Crew deliver; the Cashier settles the bill. Platform Admins handle onboarding, tenants, plans and platform operations. Different restaurants share the SaaS service, but data and operations must be isolated by restaurant scope.

App / service Local entry point Main responsibility Dependencies
customer-app http://localhost:3000 QR scanning, menu, cart, membership, tracking, wait list, reservations, group orders, markets Main API; realtime; browser storage.
admin-dashboard http://localhost:3001 Store operations, staffing, POS, service; platform onboarding review, markets, subscriptions Main API; some platform pages call management-api with a management token.
kitchen-display http://localhost:3002 Kitchen item and order preparation, offline action sync Main API; realtime; local offline storage.
management-portal http://localhost:3010 Tenants, licenses, deployments, health, markets and region policy management-api; a separate management token.
onboarding-app http://localhost:3011 Public store application, success page, application progress management-api; application lookup secret.
api http://localhost:8787 Business REST API, authentication, orders, payments, Cron, search Queue consumer Platform D1, KV, R2, Durable Object, management service binding.
management-api http://localhost:8789 Onboarding provisioning, tenants, licenses, region policy, deployment and audit retention Control-plane D1 + platform D1, KV, R2, Email Service.
realtime http://localhost:8788 WebSocket upgrade and Durable Object rooms REALTIME_SESSION; shared signing configuration and authorization data.
image-processor http://localhost:8790 Image upload, metadata, variants and image statistics Images, image D1, IMAGE_CACHE, IMAGES_BUCKET.
backup-scheduler No interactive UI / not scheduled by default Standalone Cron entry for tenant backups; the code lives in the api workers directory Platform D1, BACKUP_KV, BACKUP_STORAGE; currently crons=[].
print-agent HTTP :3003; WS :3004 Local printing, cloud claim and reporting, raw TCP printers Node, LAN printers, two keys for different purposes.

Service path of one day of operation

Customer / staff actionMain API validates and calculatesD1 stores the order and transactionsRealtime notifies the stationsKitchen → Service → CashierReceipt queued in the cloud → local agent prints

Realtime is a notification channel; D1 is the durable source of truth for orders and transactions. When notifications drop, re-read the API; do not conclude that an order or payment failed merely because a board did not update. The image service handles image files, not menu prices; management-api handles the control plane and does not replace the main API's store endpoints.

Why two "management" front ends coexist

Admin Dashboard manages the business: restaurants, menus, orders, members, POS, platform merchant recruitment and subscriptions. Management Portal manages the control plane: tenants, licenses, health, deployments and region policy. Onboarding review lives in Admin Dashboard at /dashboard/platform/onboarding, not in Management Portal. Platform market management has different entry points in the two services, so confirm which set of resources you need before integrating.

Deployment model and URLs

The currently configured default is the centrally managed platform mode DEPLOYMENT_MODE=saas. The code still contains independent, tenant license and resource provisioning capabilities, but it cannot be claimed on that basis that every new store automatically gets a dedicated URL or an independent deployment. Production domains follow each app's wrangler settings and the actual deployment; the operating examples in this handbook mostly use localhost.

Part 3 · Roles, Sign-in and Permissions

Account role, restaurant scope, modules and feature flags are conditions at different levels.

Role table

Role Role name Main entry point Scope of work
0 Platform Admin Admin Dashboard / Management Portal Platform-wide and cross-restaurant operations; store pages still require a selected restaurant context.
1 Shop Owner Admin Dashboard Own restaurant, staffing, orders, settings; shift managers currently share this role.
2 Chef Kitchen Display Own kitchen, item preparation; the schedule entry point is also in the kitchen app.
3 Service Crew Admin Dashboard /service Pick up ready orders and confirm delivery; own schedule, attendance and so on.
4 Cashier Admin Dashboard POS Take payment, shifts and receipts; POS refunds need Shop Owner / Admin approval.
5 Customer Customer App Own member profile, history and customer resources; uses the canonical customer identity.
No staff role Anonymous guest Customer App Public browsing and guest ordering; later actions rely on the single-order guest token.

Five kinds of credentials that must not be mixed

Credential How it is obtained What it can do
Staff JWT + refresh cookie Main API /auth/login Protected staff endpoints; the server also checks the active session, the user's enabled status, tokenVersion and role.
Customer JWT + refresh cookie Password, OTP or configured OAuth at /customer/auth The customer's own data and orders; grants no staff permissions.
Guest order token Guest order success response Tracking of a single order and permitted guest actions; not a pass for signing in to the whole system.
Management JWT A platform role 0 staff token exchanged via management /auth/exchange Control-plane resources; has its own issuer / audience.
Room / SSE token Main API /realtime/auth/token (staff), /auth/guest-token (guest / customer), /auth/group-token (group order members) A specified room or stream; cannot be used as a general REST Bearer token.

Staff sign-in and token refresh

  1. Open the app you belong to and enter your username and password. Chefs should go to Kitchen Display.
  2. Sign-in calls POST /api/v1/auth/login. The access token is valid for 1 hour, and the refresh token is managed in an HttpOnly cookie. Failed sign-ins are rate limited: over a 15-minute window, 10 failures from the same IP or 5 failures for the same username cause a temporary lockout.
  3. The front end redirects by role and restaurant context. When role 0 has no restaurant selected, it should first go to a platform page or pick a restaurant.
  4. When less than 3600 seconds remain on the access token, the API response carries X-Token-Refresh-Recommended: true and X-Token-Expires-In, and the existing client refreshes it; the refresh cookie must be sent with the request.
  5. If the server returns TOKEN_INVALIDATED, sign in again; you cannot simply place a self-signed JWT into the browser by hand. A valid signature must still correspond to an active sessions row.

Customer sign-in and account recovery

Customer App has sign-in, registration, forgot / reset password (/forgot-password, /reset-password), email verification (/verify-email) and a profile center; there is no separate "set password" page, so first-time setup and reset after forgetting use the same /reset-password flow. The customer API is mounted in two places: /api/v1/customer (auth, OTP, OAuth, profile and preferences) and /api/v1/customers (/me, /me/orders, /me/market-checkouts and other resources of the customer's own). They are different routers, not aliases of the same set of routes. Customer data uses customers and customer_auth_identities, separate from staff users. A person who is both staff and a customer must use each respective sign-in flow.

Whether an OTP is actually sent depends on the SMS provider; email verification and recovery depend on the Email Service; the OAuth provider list is supplied by GET /customer/auth/oauth/providers. The current code already has the OAuth entry point, callback, complete / link identity and unlink handling, but only successfully configured providers can be used. Set up the callback and provider settings following the OAuth credentials runbook.

A 403 or 404 is not necessarily a sign-in failure

Authorization usually involves, in order: signed-in identity → role → restaurant ownership → subscribed module → region policy → quota or platform-wide feature flag. MODULE_NOT_ENABLED is a plan / module problem; MODULE_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION is region policy; QUOTA_EXCEEDED is usage; a feature that is not enabled may return 404 directly. Do not redirect every error to sign-in again.

Safe operating habits

  • When staff leave or change roles: an authorized person disables / adjusts the account; the server checks the latest data and session.
  • Guest tokens, application secrets, set-password links and print cloud keys should all be kept as credentials; support records should keep only identifiers, never paste full secrets.
  • A button hidden in the front end is only navigation; back-end authorization decides whether an action may run.
  • Browser staff writes may need a CSRF cookie and the matching header. On a 403, check Origin, cookie and CSRF rather than turning protection off.

Part 4 · How One Order Travels Through the System

Fulfillment status, item status and payment status are stored separately; a successful payment is the payment service's responsibility.

A worked example of the main flow

A customer orders two dishes at table A1. The customer app submits the cart; the API validates the restaurant, table, options, prices, coupons and inventory, and creates the order. After the restaurant confirms it, the kitchen sees it. The first dish starts being prepared and the parent order moves to preparing; when all items are done, the parent order moves to ready. Service Crew pick up the order and confirm delivery. The Cashier takes payment in the POS, PaymentService creates the transaction and settles the order, and finally a receipt is issued and handed to print-agent.

pending (awaiting confirmation)confirmed (accepted)preparing (in preparation)ready (awaiting delivery)delivered (delivered)

paid is produced by the payment flow.Currently the ordinary PUT /orders/:id/status does not allow an order to be changed directly to paid; a button or external integration must not declare money received merely by changing the fulfillment status. The payment flow can settle at different fulfillment stages depending on payment conditions, so the sequence above must not be read as "payment is only possible after delivery".

Statuses and valid operations

Status Meaning Reachable from the ordinary status endpoint
pending Order created, awaiting acceptance confirmed / cancelled
confirmed Accepted; can be sent to the kitchen preparing / cancelled
preparing Preparation has started ready / cancelled
ready Whole order is prepared, awaiting handover delivered / cancelled
delivered Handover complete refunded is valid within ORDER_STATUS_TRANSITIONS, but no role in ROLE_STATUS_PERMISSIONS can set refunded, so PUT /orders/:id/status returns 403; refunds always go through the refund endpoint. Payment settlement goes through the payment service.
paid Settled by the payment flow The ordinary status endpoint has no next step; refunds use the dedicated refund flow.
cancelled Cancelled The ordinary status endpoint has no next step.
refunded Refund-related terminal state The ordinary status endpoint has no next step.

Who can set what through the ordinary status endpoint

Role Currently allowed target statuses
0 Platform Admin pending, confirmed, preparing, ready, delivered, cancelled
1 Shop Owner confirmed, preparing, ready, delivered, cancelled
2 Chef preparing, ready
3 Service Crew delivered
4 Cashier confirmed

A role being allowed a target does not mean it can skip status transitions or restaurant ownership. Delivery has its own pickup check; the Shop Owner has a deliver-on-behalf exception. Refund permissions and payment settlement are different contracts from this table.

Three status axes

  • orders.status: fulfillment / terminal state of the whole order.
  • order_items.status: per-item preparation status. After an item update, the current KitchenService re-checks the parent order and advances preparing / ready through OrdersService.
  • orders.payment_status, payment transaction and refund record: payment, failure, partial refund and so on. The API's order payment success status uses completed; the transaction layer may use paid, so do not mix them into one enum.

Side effects after a successful write

A status update carries a version check, saves the corresponding timestamp, then invalidates the cache and broadcasts. confirmed tries to create a kitchen ticket. Flows such as delivered / paid handle releasing the table or the guest's active lock. A failed broadcast or print queueing does not mean the persisted order is revoked; query the order and ticket for the actual result.

Repeated operations and concurrency

  • Two people editing the same order:may return 409 ORDER_VERSION_CONFLICT; re-read the current state before deciding, rather than overwriting unconditionally. The client's version is only compared when the update carries expectedVersion (such as adding items, removing items, discounts); the status endpoint reads the current version on the server, and conflicts only when someone else changed it between the read and the write.
  • Same guest resubmitting:reuse clientMutationId to avoid creating duplicate orders; after a success, query the original order.
  • Kitchen replaying the same status:the current KitchenService treats it as a safe replay and still checks the parent order. This is not the same contract as the ordinary order status endpoint.
  • Cancellation:conditional status and inventory compensation prevent double restocking; a delivered order must not be treated as unfulfilled and cancelled.
  • Refunds:keep the payment transaction and refund record; do not change an order to cancelled as a substitute for a refund.

Where amounts come from

The cart shows an estimate; the server recalculates using the menu, options and settings. Amounts are stored as integer cents, while some fields in the payment API still use major currency units, so integrations must convert according to the schema and must not put cents directly into amount. Cross-restaurant analytics are grouped by currency; TWD, MYR and VND must not be added together directly.

  • Every money field stores integer cents (major unit × 100) for all currencies, TWD included: NT$155 is stored as 15500, and only 15500 is valid (15550 is not a valid TWD amount).
  • The currency is decided by the server from the restaurant settings. A currency in the request is only compared; a mismatch returns 400 CURRENCY_MISMATCH; an amount whose precision does not fit the currency (such as TWD with fractional units) returns 400 CURRENCY_PRECISION.
  • A payment's registerId and shiftId must be sent together; using the same Idempotency-Key on a different order returns 422 IDEMPOTENCY_ORDER_MISMATCH.
  • Cancelling an order (DELETE /api/v1/orders/:id) is limited to role 0 / 1 and may carry an optional reason (over 500 characters is truncated, not rejected); a Cashier (role 4) cannot cancel.
  • The kitchen ticket (the receipts table with receiptType=kitchen, used by Print Agent to print the paper ticket) is created when the status becomes confirmed; a creation failure is only logged (the order is not rolled back, there is no alert and no automatic re-issue), so a confirmed order may have no kitchen ticket. Kitchen Display lists orders by order status and does not read tickets, so the Chef's screen is unaffected; only restaurants that print paper tickets are affected, and need to check in the order details. Known gap: the wait list pre-order confirmation (confirmWaitingListPreOrders) batch-changes orders directly to confirmed and does not create kitchen tickets.

Part 5 · Customer App

From scanning and choosing food to submitting, tracking, membership, wait list and group ordering.

Pages and entry points

Path / feature What the reader wants to accomplish Conditions
/, /discover, /markets, /markets/:slug Explore restaurants, markets and dishes Public; content depends on live restaurants, markets and sellable data.
/scan, /order Scan a code or resolve a signed entry The camera needs browser permission; the QR must be currently valid and the resource enabled.
/restaurant/:restaurantId/table/:tableId Dine-in table menu The table belongs to that restaurant; a seat QR also carries seat information.
/restaurant/:restaurantId/shop/order-type, /shop/menu Choose takeaway / delivery and order Restaurant mode and sellable settings.
/orders/:id, /restaurant/:restaurantId/table/:tableId/order/:orderId, /restaurant/:restaurantId/shop/order/:orderId Track a single order (three entry points: member history, dine-in table, takeaway / delivery) The member's own identity or the matching guest token. The table and shop paths share the same order tracking screen.
/restaurant/:restaurantId/table/:tableId/cart View and submit the dine-in cart The table belongs to that restaurant; the cart is local data and does not count as an order until submission succeeds and an order number is returned.
/login, /register, /profile, /orders Member sign-in, profile setup, history A genuine customer identity; notification provider per configuration.
/r/:restaurantId/wait-list Join the wait list The restaurant has enabled the wait list; enter name, party size and phone.
/r/:restaurantId/wait-list/:ticketId View your own ticket: status, estimated wait in minutes, name and party size Ticket number and access credential; do not repost publicly. The page refreshes automatically until the ticket reaches a final state; it does not refresh while the tab is in the background, so switch back and look again.
/r/:restaurantId/wait-list/history Look up your own wait list history at that restaurant by phone; click an entry to return to that ticket A phone number is required; when that phone needs verification (including the server returning 403), the page takes the phone to the SMS OTP mode of /login and returns here after verification. This is the flow, not a broken wait list system.
/markets/:slug/checkout/:checkoutId Market multi-vendor checkout tracking: processing / submitted, each vendor's sub-order, total, deduction and amount due, payment Opening each vendor's sub-order needs the matching guest token; the page tries to recover it and, on failure, shows that the sub-order cannot be accessed instead of failing the whole page. The payment status can be paid, failed or partial_paid; when the market checkout feature is disabled or online payment is unavailable, the pay button is disabled and a notice is shown.
/about, /privacy, /terms About, privacy policy, terms of service Public static pages, no sign-in needed; content follows the i18n locale.
Any other path (/:pathMatch(.*)*) Shows "Page not found" A mistyped URL, an old sticker or an expired link lands here; it is a front-end catch-all and does not mean the API returned 404.
/restaurant/:restaurantId/reserve Online reservation The current router already has ReservationView; older documents saying there is no screen are out of date.
/restaurant/:restaurantId/services/:serviceItemId/book Book a service Service enabled, payment conditions and slot capacity.
/group/:shareCode, /group/order/:groupOrderId Join a group order, shared cart Share code, member identity, host controls.

Dine-in ordering: step by step

  1. Scan the QR on the table or seat. Confirm the restaurant name, table number and seat on screen; if they do not match, stop and ask staff to check the sticker.
  2. Browse categories, items, prices and sold-out status. Open an item, choose the quantity, required options and add-ons; use the note only for requests, not as a price change.
  3. Add to the cart; in the cart, confirm again the items, options, quantities, contact details and coupons.
  4. After submitting, wait for the server's response. Only when an order number and the tracking page appear is the order considered created; on a network timeout, check the original order first to avoid creating new orders repeatedly.
  5. Keep the tracking link and the guest token in the browser. Clearing data, changing device or private mode may lose the single-order authorization.
  6. Track pending confirmation, in preparation, ready for pickup / awaiting delivery, delivered and payment information. When the status does not move, reload from the API and give the order number to staff.

Takeaway and delivery

A shop QR or the discovery page can enter shop mode; it is a public restaurant identifier, not proof of presence or a member sign-in credential. After the restaurant regenerates its QR, ordering from an old sticker may return SHOP_QR_REVOKED. Delivery must provide an address and phone; whether it is supported, the fees and the service area depend on the restaurant's settings and the currently available flow; the presence of delivery fields must not be read as meaning courier tracking or a logistics platform is connected.

Modifying, adding to and cancelling

A guest's single order and its additions each carry 1–20 item lines, with a quantity of at most 99 per line; additions are only allowed while the order is pending or confirmed, and the whole guest order may not exceed 20 item lines in total (exceeding that returns 400). Once preparation has started, do not repeatedly "modify" an already submitted order from the local cart; the cart and an order that has been created are different data. Whether cancellation is allowed is decided by the server's status rules and the order credential. If a paid order needs a refund, an authorized staff member should run the refund flow.

Members versus guests

Guests can order without registering. Members can view their own history and profile center; the current guest entry can recognize an optional canonical customer token and saves the customerId, and member ordering also has its own path. A staff account cannot be used as a substitute for verifying a customer member. The Customer App's access token is held in memory and restored after a reload by the HttpOnly refresh cookie, so "no JWT found in localStorage" should not be taken as sign-in being broken.

Wait list, reservations and service bookings

  1. Wait list:choose the party size, fill in the details, get a ticket number and keep the lookup credential. Registering the same active wait list entry again may read back the original ticket.
  2. Calling a number:after the restaurant calls the number there is a 5-minute confirmation deadline; the customer confirms arrival on screen, and a confirmation after the timeout is treated as expired. When expired, register again under the restaurant's rules.
  3. Wait list pre-order:pick food first from a valid wait list entry; the order is formally accepted and the kitchen notified only when the party is seated.
  4. Reservations:choose a bookable date / slot and party size and keep the confirmation code; a reservation is not a food order or a payment.
  5. Service bookings:read the service slots, prices and pay-at-venue / deposit / prepayment conditions, and keep the confirmation code and, if needed, the calendar information. If a payment route is not enabled, follow the screen and the restaurant's instructions; a successful booking must not be taken as a successful payment.

Group ordering

Multi-person ordering at the same restaurant: host opens the group → shares the link → members join → each adds dishes → host checks and submits / locks the order → it converges into one master order → tracking. Members use a member token, not a staff JWT. After the order is locked it can no longer be edited as an active cart. There are two different lists for splitting the bill: the split operation (splitBillSchema) accepts equal, proportional, individual, by_item and custom; the split preference the host saves (splitTypePreferenceSchema) accepts only equal, by_item and proportional, because custom and single_payer need per-member amounts and a group order has no field to store them. But "calculating the split amounts" and "actually receiving each member's money" must be reconciled separately. On finalizing_failed, the real order may already exist; have the platform investigate before rebuilding.

Market multi-vendor checkout

One checkout corresponds to one child order per vendor, which differs from group ordering's single same-restaurant master order. Creating across vendors validates each vendor's eligibility, and a mid-way failure is compensated. Applying a platform coupon is handled before payment; payment must have a usable provider. If online payment is not configured, the payment is rejected and is not pretended to be paid. Each vendor may finish at a different time, so check pickup and payment status vendor by vendor.

Boundaries of offline use and notifications

Browser caching can keep some already loaded data, but it cannot guarantee creating new orders offline, real-time inventory or payment. Customer Web Push depends on CUSTOMER_WEB_PUSH_ENABLED, VAPID, the front-end public key and acceptance of actual delivery; without that configuration, do not rely on background push to call numbers. Keep the tracking page open or follow the restaurant's on-site calling.

Common customer errors

Symptom Meaning and next step
QR invalid / 404 Ask staff for the current QR; do not edit the tableId yourself.
Item removed, insufficient stock / 409 Re-read the menu and cart, remove items that cannot be sold, then confirm again.
INVALID_CUSTOMIZATION Fill in the required options and respect the selectable count; the server does not accept arbitrary surcharges.
ACTIVE_GUEST_ORDER_EXISTS This device already has an unsettled order at the restaurant; open the original tracking page and do not work around it with a new device.
CLIENT_MUTATION_DUPLICATE This submission was already processed; check the original result.
Payment provider not configured Choose an on-site payment the restaurant supports, or ask the restaurant to check the configuration; do not retry it into paid.
Member email / SMS not received First check the details and resend limits; the operator checks the provider, and a page notice must not be taken as real delivery.

Suggested customer acceptance testing: test ordinary table and seat QR codes separately; test members and guests separately; then test sold-out, resubmission, crossing midnight, tracking dropouts, cancellation and real payment callbacks.

Part 6 · Admin Dashboard (Restaurant Back Office)

The Shop Owner's operations center, which also hosts service, cashiering and some platform features.

Setup order for opening a store for the first time

  1. Account and restaurant:Use the activated account to set a password and sign in, and confirm the restaurant name, country, currency and time zone. A new restaurant may stay unable to take orders at first, and opens only once setup is complete.
  2. Basic details:Maintain contact details, address, opening hours and images. The information used by public discovery must be real data.
  3. Menu:First create categories, then items, prices, sellable status and option groups. Items that carry a surcharge or are mandatory use option data, not just a note.
  4. Tables and QR:Create the real table numbers, capacity and seat mode; print and check the stickers. A table record's id is different from a table number such as A1 shown in the store.
  5. Order settings:Confirm allowGuestOrders, shop mode, minimum spend, tax and service charge, auto-accept, and the pickup methods actually supported.
  6. Staff and stations:Create Chef, Service Crew and Cashier accounts; verify role and restaurant station by station, and do not share one admin account for all daily operations.
  7. POS and printing:Create / enable the cash register, open a shift, pair the counter and kitchen agents, and complete physical print acceptance.
  8. Trial order:Use a customer's browser to scan the on-site QR and go through order → accept → prepare → deliver → cash payment → receipt → shift close, then open for business.

Main page map

Feature Current entry point Operating notes
Operations dashboard /dashboard, /dashboard/owner-overview Date range, restaurant context, active order volume; analytics data cannot be used as evidence of an individual payment.
Daily stall opening /dashboard/market-open-report A market stall reports the day's trading information; this is different from the whole restaurant's isActive.
Orders /dashboard/orders Only role 0 / 1 / 3 / 4 can enter. Filter, details, confirm, valid cancellation, export; rely on the response's version / status.
Back-office kitchen view /dashboard/kitchen role 0 / 1 / 2; a different entry point from the Kitchen Display app.
Menu and options /dashboard/menu, /dashboard/menu/option-groups Maintain prices, images, inventory, sellable status and option bindings.
Tables / seats /dashboard/seating/table-setup Real table numbers, capacity, QR mode; do not treat a manual release as payment received. The single-table detail is /dashboard/seating/tables/:id (role 0 / 1).
Reservations / wait list /dashboard/seating, /waiting-list, /queue-dashboard (all under seating) Confirm bookings, call numbers, seat and cancel; the two capacity rule sets must be coordinated.
Staffing /dashboard/employees, with its attendance / scheduling / leaves sub-pages Employees, scheduling, attendance, leave; see Part 9 for details. There are also /dashboard/employees/scheduling/advanced and /scheduling/analytics (role 0 / 1).
Employee self-service /dashboard/my-shifts, my-leaves, my-attendance Open to role 0–4, to check one's own schedule, leave and attendance; Chefs (who cannot use the admin dashboard) use the kitchen's /my-shifts.
Cashiering /dashboard/pos/checkout, /dashboard/pos/management Shifts, payment, refund submission and reconciliation; see Part 8 for details.
Print agents /dashboard/print-agents Issue / revoke the cloud key, distinguishing counter agents from store-wide agents.
Ingredients and forecasting /dashboard/ingredients, forecast Maintain recipes, manual stocktaking and demand forecasts; an order does not automatically deduct ingredients.
Members and reviews /dashboard/members, reviews The restaurant's member relationships / loyalty and order reviews; avoid mixing with the platform-wide customer directory.
Operational analytics and AI /dashboard/analytics, /dashboard/ai-analytics/config, /dashboard/ai-analytics/insights, /dashboard/ai-analytics/products (role 0 and 1 only) Dates, currency, data quality and provider configuration.
Coupons and group orders /dashboard/coupons, group-orders Coupon thresholds, validity period, quota; view the restaurant's group orders.
Service bookings /dashboard/service-bookings Service settings, booking capacity, arrival confirmation and completion.
Support tickets /dashboard/feedback The restaurant reports problems to the platform; these are not customer reviews.
Announcements /dashboard/broadcasts Restaurant announcements / push; actual channels and delivery depend on configuration.
Subscription, settings and monitoring /dashboard/billing, settings, monitoring Feature modules, currency and business settings, monitoring readings.

Opening, trading and closing each day

Opening:Check that the restaurant can take orders, the menu is sellable and remaining quantities are right; confirm the kitchen and service stations, the Cashier's active shift, the agents and printers; if at a market, complete the day's stall-opening data. During service:Handle pending orders, watch for overdue preparation and a backlog of ready orders; mark items sold out promptly; keep the order number for refunds and exceptions. Closing:Handle unsettled orders and pending refund approvals, count the cash drawer and close the shift; confirm there are no tickets waiting to print or in an uncertain state, then close order intake according to operating rules.

Menu and inventory

  1. Create items with the restaurant's own categories; the price and the original price must be consistent, and do not apply another restaurant's category id.
  2. Bind option groups and set required, maximum / minimum selectable counts and surcharges, so customers can submit with structured data.
  3. Once an item is taken off the menu, new orders can no longer buy it; orders already created use their line-item snapshot and are not repriced because the menu changed.
  4. Item inventory and ingredient inventory are separate. A single order deducts item quantity with a conditional update; ingredient recipes are currently used mainly for forecasting and manual management.
  5. When several managers edit the same item, only sending updatedAt gives optimistic locking on that path; on a 409, read it back and edit again.

Replacing a QR

Table QR rotation uses prepare → print / stick on → activate. After prepare the old code is still valid; activate is what invalidates the old code. If you do not want to replace it, discard the pending code. Regenerating the restaurant's shop QR also retires the old code; swap the stickers at the same time and test the public discovery entry. A QR signature and version cannot be substituted by hand-editing the URL.

Extended store features

  • Members:The platform's customers is one person; restaurant_customers is that person's relationship with a restaurant. A restaurant manages only its own relationship data.
  • Reviews:Reviews are created under an order identity; the public list and the restaurant management list have different authorization.
  • Support tickets:Provide the problem, time of occurrence, app, order number and error code; do not paste secrets or full personal data.
  • AI:Configure and test the provider first, then generate insights; when the statistics are incomplete, do not treat a model's answer as a financial ledger.
  • Delivery / wallet integrations:Encrypted credentials, webhook, adapter and provider readiness are all required; having a settings page does not mean transactions will succeed.

Pages for Platform Admins in the same app

/dashboard/platform is the platform overview; /platform/markets, /platform/market-checkouts, /platform/customers, /platform/onboarding all sit under dashboard and handle business-side platform management. There are also /dashboard/account-management and /dashboard/subscriptions. These are not the same resources as the Management Portal's tenants / licenses pages.

Entry points and redirects not listed on the map

  • /forgot-password, /reset-password: Admin Dashboard's own forgot / reset password pages (a Shop Owner setting a password after approval also goes through here).
  • /owner → /dashboard/owner-overview; /cashier → /dashboard/pos/checkout; /dashboard/queue → SeatingQueueDashboard.
  • /dashboard/waiting/dashboard → SeatingQueueDashboard; /dashboard/waiting, /dashboard/waiting/list, /dashboard/waiting-list → SeatingWaitingList; /dashboard/reservations → SeatingReservations. Old bookmarks and old documents that mention wait list paths all land on these routes, and the current screens are under Seating.
  • /unauthorized: when the sign-in is valid but the role or module does not allow entering the page, the router sends the user to this "insufficient permissions" page. It is the front-end counterpart of a 403, not an expired sign-in; use an account with permission, or ask the Shop Owner / Platform Admin to enable it. People who are not signed in are sent to /login, and the page they wanted to return to is remembered.
  • Any other nonexistent URL shows "Page not found" (the NotFound catch-all), which is a different situation from /unauthorized.
  • role 2 (Chef) cannot use the admin dashboard: entering the dashboard home signs the user out and redirects to Kitchen Display.

Troubleshooting permissions and empty pages

Check in order: account role, the signed-in user's restaurant, the role 0 selected restaurant context, subscription row, module, region policy, then look at the network response. A permission notice when basic has not bought a module is expected; a blank list may be a date, filter, pagination or simply no data yet, and it cannot be inferred directly that the API is broken. Old paths such as /tables, /users, /scheduling and /leaves may be only redirects; rely on the current router and sidebar.

Part 7 · Kitchen Display

Preparation is item by item and the server checks whole-order progress; when offline, actions are retained, but the sync result must not be ignored.

Pages and required conditions

The entry point is /login, and the main board is /kitchen/:restaurantId; there are also /my-shifts, /settings and /history. The /kitchen/:restaurantId and /my-shifts routes require requiredRole 2; /settings and /history only require sign-in at the route level, but the auth store rejects accounts that are not role 2 at sign-in, so in practice only Chefs can get in. The Chef role is 2; the user must belong to the correct restaurant, and that restaurant must have kitchen_display effectively enabled. The server allows role 0 / 1 / 2 / 3 for some kitchen data, but that does not mean the kitchen app offers the same entry point to every role.

/unauthorized (the insufficient-permissions page, with a "sign in again" button that returns to /login): shown when the user is signed in but the role the route requires is not 2, or the :restaurantId in the URL differs from the restaurant the signed-in account belongs to (the board checks this again when it loads). The remedy is to confirm the account's restaurant, use the correct restaurant's URL, or sign in again; if not signed in, the user is always sent to /login first and the original page is remembered. Any other nonexistent URL shows "Page does not exist" (the catch-all). Both are front-end screens and are unrelated to whether the API is healthy.

From accepting an order to serving

  1. Sign in and confirm the board's restaurant and connection. The work queue contains only confirmed, preparing and ready; pending orders are first confirmed by the restaurant or auto-accepted.
  2. Read the order number, table / seat, pickup method, quantity, size, options, add-ons and notes. A UUID is an internal identifier, not the on-site table number.
  3. Press start preparation per item or per order. The item moves to preparing, and the server uses the latest item and parent order status to advance the whole order.
  4. Mark items ready when done; when the last item is ready and the parent order is in preparing, the server advances the whole order to ready and saves the ready time.
  5. Confirm the API response and the board status. Once the food is ready, hand it to Service Crew / the pickup area; a Chef must not change an order directly to paid or use ready in place of delivery.

Real-time channels and connection indicators

Order events go through the WebSocket kitchen:{restaurantId} Durable Object room. There is also the /kitchen/:restaurantId/events SSE, which currently sends only connected and heartbeats. A board showing one channel as connected does not guarantee that all WebSocket order events get through; if a new order does not appear, re-fetch the queue and check REST, SSE and WebSocket separately.

Offline operation

The kitchen offlineService can cache orders and queued actions and replay them when the connection is restored. While offline, others may already have cancelled, settled or advanced the order; the server's restaurant, status and version checks still apply. Each queued action is retried at most 5 times (MAX_RETRY_ATTEMPTS); when a replay is rejected, find out why and verify the dish manually, and do not retry indefinitely. Switching restaurant clears the previous tenant's offline data, to avoid cross-restaurant resending.

Repeated completion and multiple boards

Replaying the same status for the same item does not write again, but still checks the parent order, so an offline retry after a lost response can recover. If different items complete at the same time and hit a parent order version conflict, the server re-reads once to confirm whether the other side has already made the required advancement. This does not mean the full "two kitchens racing for an order / missing ingredient handling" product flow has been accepted.

Taking items off the menu and notes

On the permitted menu paths, a Chef can change only the sellable status and item inventory, not prices or categories. Internal kitchen notes should stay in the kitchen data / ticket; the customer receipt must not mix in internal content. For missing ingredients, customer order changes or preparation exceptions, coordinate with the Shop Owner first; this handbook does not assume a complete missing-ingredient reporting and refund integration exists.

Troubleshooting

Symptom Order of checks
No orders after sign-in Restaurant context → is the order confirmed → module → API queue → realtime.
All dishes done, but the service side still cannot see it Check whether the parent order is ready, and readyAt; re-fetch the list. Do not follow the old documents' "items never propagate".
KITCHEN_ITEM_SCOPE_DENIED The item / order / restaurant combination does not match, or the order is no longer within the range the kitchen allows.
Offline sync failed Look at the queue and the server's latest status; the order may already be cancelled or settled.
Screen reloads after a deployment The recovery mechanism for renamed chunk files; sign in again and check the actions waiting to sync.

Acceptance should include: starting / completing two dishes item by item, same-value retry, simultaneous completion on different devices, replay after cancellation, cleanup on switching restaurants, and a real WebSocket disconnect and reconnect.

Part 8 · Cashiering, Payments, Refunds and Shift Close

Checkout is recorded through transactions and shifts; cash, card and electronic payments affect the cash drawer differently.

Entry points and preparation

Use Admin Dashboard's /dashboard/pos/checkout cashier page and /dashboard/pos/management management page. role 0 / 1 / 4 operate according to endpoint permissions; among them GET /pos/shifts/stats is open only to role 0 / 1. The register and shift must belong to the same restaurant and be bound correctly; a payment cannot carry just a registerId or just a shiftId (registerId and shiftId must be sent together, otherwise 400, see payments/routes/index.ts).

Opening a shift

  1. Select / enable the actual cash register.
  2. Count the opening cash, enter the actual amount and open the shift.
  3. Confirm the server response shows the active shift and the machine binding; the same register cannot have two active shifts at the same time.
  4. If you want receipts, first confirm the receipt_printing module, the agent and the printer.

Taking a single payment

  1. Bring up the order and confirm the restaurant, order number, the total calculated by the server and the current payment status.
  2. Choose the actual payment method; the methods available are limited by country / currency and provider configuration.
  3. The POS submission carries registerId, shiftId and Idempotency-Key; the amount matches what the server can collect. A partial payment must use the matching paymentMode and payments array contract.
  4. For cash, check the money received and the change; for card / wallet, check the real transaction result, and do not treat a page redirect succeeding as the provider having credited the money.
  5. After the server creates the transaction and settles, read back the order and transaction status; then open the receipt.

When unsure whether a payment succeeded, first check the transaction status and re-check / safely resend with the original idempotency key. Charging again with a different idempotency key may become a new transaction.

Cash drawer and revenue

totalSales counts every payment method; cashSales, cardSales and digitalSales are separate buckets. Cash sales write a sale cash flow, while cards and e-wallets do not add cash to the drawer. So "today's revenue" should not be taken as equal to "the cash currently in the drawer". Manual deposits / withdrawals, refunds and shift close must all be explained by the corresponding records.

POS refunds

  1. Look up the original order and the refundable amount, and enter the reason and the actual refund method.
  2. A POS refund request carries X-Register-Id and X-Shift-Id, and the server checks the same restaurant and shift.
  3. Only refunds created by a Cashier (role 4) stop at processing, awaiting Admin / Owner approval; refunds initiated by role 0 / 1 themselves complete immediately without review. Submitting for approval does not by itself mean the money has been returned.
  4. Approve, reject and cancel (POST /pos/refunds/:id/approve|reject|cancel) are available only to role 0 / 1; a Cashier cannot approve on their own. Admin / Owner approval has the finalizer update the original order, refund statistics and any qualifying cash flow; they may also reject / cancel per the rules.
  5. If the original shift has ended, record a post-close adjustment; do not silently rewrite a closed shift's cash drawer.
  6. After a refund, check the refund record, orders.payment_status, refundAmountCents and the provider result, not just a single "refund completed" message.

Three kinds of refund must not be mixed

Path Purpose Main conditions
/pos/refunds/create + approve / reject / cancel POS approval and shift accounts create is role 0 / 1 / 4; a Cashier (role 4) must submit for approval, role 0 / 1 complete immediately; approve / reject / cancel are role 0 / 1 only.
/payments/refund Refund of a known payment transaction role 0 / 1 / 4; transaction and limit, provider support.
/market-checkouts/:id/refund Market multi-vendor refund Platform role 0; checked against the checkout, sub-transactions and revenue-share mode.

Closing a shift

Stop new cashier operations, check pending refunds, then count physically. Shift close must have the operator enter the actual amount; entering 0 is valid, but 0 or the system's expected figure must not be filled in automatically. 

expected cash = opening cash + cash sales − approved cash refunds ± manual cash movements ± cash rounding adjustment
difference    = counted cash − expected cash

Example: opening 1,000, cash received 510, approved cash refund 50, no other movements, so the expected figure is 1,460; counted 1,450, a difference of −10. Card / wallet sales are not added into this formula. Source records such as closing / opening / sale must not all be added again, otherwise they are double counted.

Cash rounding adjustment occurs only in MYR: when paying with physical cash, the amount received is rounded to the nearest 5 sen (PaymentService collectableAmount). The order total does not change; the difference is stored in the payment's roundingAdjustmentCents; ReportService adds cashRoundingAdjustment to the expected cash. Example: MYR 10.33 paid in cash as 10.35, a rounding adjustment of +0.02, expected cash is 0.02 higher. For TWD and other currencies, and for card / wallet, the adjustment is 0, so the example above is unaffected.

Common errors and acceptance

Error / symptom Handling
ORDER_NOT_PAYABLE The original order is already settled, cannot be paid or is not in a valid payment status; read it back before deciding.
PAYMENT_TOTAL_MISMATCH (expectedTotal differs from the server's collectable amount, 409) / PARTIAL_PAYMENT_TOTAL_MISMATCH (the partial payments' sum does not equal the order total) / PAYMENT_AMOUNT_MISMATCH (amount mismatch, 409) Stop the payment, and check the server total, units and the partial payment allocation. AMOUNT_MISMATCH belongs to the market checkout and webhook / reconciliation paths; it is not a POS payment error code.
Missing Idempotency-Key Supply the unique key for the same payment, and do not let each network retry generate a different key.
IDEMPOTENCY_ORDER_MISMATCH (422) The same Idempotency-Key was already used on a different order; each order and each payment intent uses its own key.
Refund over the limit Refunds that are completed and processing both take up the limit; check unfinished refunds first.
Register already has an active shift Read the existing shift; do not reopen or rebind another restaurant's shift.
Shift close has a difference Keep the actual amount, the reason and the records, and handle it under the restaurant's review process.

Basic acceptance requires actually walking through cash payment, change, partial payment, resending twice with the same key, refund submission / approval, a refund after the shift is closed and a shift close difference. Real card / wallet, callbacks and returned funds additionally need real testing on the provider's side; printing a receipt also does not mean an electronic invoice has been lawfully issued.

Part 9 · Service, Wait List and Staffing

On-site handover, seating arrangements and staff schedules work together in the back office.

Service station

The entry point is Admin Dashboard /service, not a standalone Service App. role 0 / 1 / 3 can enter the screen (but only 0 / 3 can use the claim endpoint); the server uses the orders feature, and there is no ninth delivering order status.

  1. Read the ready list and confirm priority, table / seat, items and waiting time.
  2. Start delivery by calling POST /orders/:id/delivery-claim (role 0 / 3 only; a Shop Owner, role 1, cannot claim); the server saves deliveryAssignedTo and deliveryStartTime.
  3. Check the food, then take it to the correct table / pickup location.
  4. To confirm delivery, send delivered to PUT /orders/:id/status. Only the person who claimed can complete delivery; the Shop Owner (role 1) is exempt from claiming and can deliver directly on behalf, still subject to the restaurant and status limits. A Platform Admin (role 0) is not in this exception and must claim first, otherwise it returns DELIVERY_CLAIM_REQUIRED.
  5. If there is a claim conflict or the order has changed, read it back. Do not conclude that the server has assigned it just because the browser's localPhase was changed.

The list awaiting delivery currently polls every 15 seconds; it is not a real-time WebSocket subscription. sessionStorage can keep some screen phases, but the server fields are the source of the claim. Today's delivered list still has documented limits on date / status and pagination: orders created across midnight, paid after delivery or spanning more than one page all need extra checking, and the list numbers must not be used directly as a complete performance report.

Wait list calling and seating

  1. After a guest takes a number, the restaurant looks at the active wait list and party sizes.
  2. Choose an available table with enough capacity and call the number; the ticket moves to called; the confirmation deadline is 5 minutes, and a confirmation after the timeout triggers expireWaiting and returns "call has timed out", so the guest must queue again. Staff operations (query, call, seat, expire, batch call) are limited to role 0 / 1 / 3 / 4; statistics are limited to role 0 / 1.
  3. The customer confirms / arrives directly, and staff mark seated through the permitted path.
  4. Seating handles the wait list pre-order and notifies the kitchen; do not re-enter the same pre-order as a new order.
  5. No-show, expired or cancelled are handled by the ticket rules, and table occupancy is checked.

Reservations versus service bookings

A reservation holds a table slot; a service booking holds a service item's slot capacity and payment conditions; the wait list is the on-site queue. /queue is a compatibility entry for the wait list service, not another set of data: Admin Dashboard's /queue is just a redirect to SeatingQueueDashboard; the API's /api/v1/queue delegates to WaitingListService through UnifiedQueueService. A reservation's confirm / no-show is limited to role 0 / 1 / 4, while arrive / seat / complete are also open to role 3. These three kinds should not share one "complete" button to explain all behavior. Seating a reservation does not mean a food order has been created, and the table capacity of the wait list and reservations also needs on-site coordination.

Staff accounts

The Shop Owner creates the restaurant's staff, chooses the role and enabled status, and hands over the sign-in method. Disabling affects existing token / session validation. Do not turn someone into a Platform Admin just so that staff can see data for several restaurants; users currently belong to a single restaurantId, and it must not be claimed that a multi-branch Shop Owner organization is supported.

Scheduling and shift swaps

  1. Maintain shift templates, employee availability and time off.
  2. Create single / batch shifts and check for conflicts such as overlapping shifts and leave conflicts.
  3. Employees view their own arrangements through my-shifts; the three self-service pages my-shifts, my-leaves and my-attendance are open to role 0–4. The shift swap flow is: the other employee first accepts (POST /swap-requests/:id/accept), then role 0 / 1 approves or rejects; the requester also has an independent cancel.
  4. After a supervisor handles conflicts and swaps, re-confirm the actual people and times.

A leave request approved afterwards may conflict with an already scheduled shift; do not assume that, just because checks ran when the schedule was created, every later change will be rescheduled automatically. The Chef's schedule entry is in Kitchen Display, to avoid being blocked by the admin router's role redirect.

Attendance

Employees clock in / clock out against their own shifts. Clocking in twice, clocking out without clocking in, and clocking out twice are rejected. A missed punch is back-filled by an authorized supervisor with the reason recorded; do not assume the system will fill it in automatically. After clocking out, the actual hours and overtime calculation must be checked against the shift and the restaurant's date / time zone.

Leave and balances

Maintain leave types and annual balances. remaining = totalDays − usedDays − pendingDays; submitting a request first takes up pending, and approve / reject / cancel then update it. The reviewer must be an active Admin / Owner, and a Shop Owner reviews only their own restaurant. A balance adjustment and a per-entry adjustment history are not the same thing; keep any necessary external explanation according to what the current records can capture.

Data to leave behind at on-site handover

  • Undelivered order numbers, the current claimant and the location of exceptions.
  • Wait list parties not yet seated, and upcoming reservations / service bookings.
  • Registers with unclosed shifts and processing refunds.
  • Sold-out items, kitchen backlog and printer status.
  • The day's attendance exceptions and shift staff; do not treat an "online account" as having clocked in.

Part 10 · Print Agent and Physical Printing

Cloud ticket → local claim → real TCP transfer → result report.

Printing is not the browser printing straight to the printer

The cloud generates a receipts row and queues it as pending; the resident in-store Node agent actively polls and claims; the driver sends ESC/POS or supported Star commands to the network printer, then reports back. Behind NAT / a firewall, the cloud does not need to reach into in-store devices. The current production transport is raw TCP, usually on 9100; USB, serial and Bluetooth must not be treated as implemented just because their names are listed in configuration: LocalPrintService's discovery default connectionTypes is ["usb","network"], but PrinterDriverFactory's USB scan is an empty implementation (it returns an empty array); the serial scan only probes the default port, and detectPrinter returns no device for any non-network connection; Bluetooth has no scan implementation. In practice only network printers can be found and printed to.

Two kinds of agent

Binding Tickets received Typical use
Bound to a registerId That register's receipts Counter receipts.
Not bound to a registerId Tickets with register_id IS NULL Store-wide / kitchen tickets.

The restaurant and register pairing is decided by the cloud credential; an agent cannot obtain another restaurant's jobs by self-reporting a restaurantId. A kitchen ticket is automatically attempted when an order becomes confirmed, and one is not opened again if a non-cancelled ticket already exists. The kitchen ticket of a cancelled order is voided when claimed.

Startup steps

  1. Prepare a reachable network printer and confirm the IP, port, command mode, paper width / character columns and encoding.
  2. The Owner / Admin issues a cloud key at /dashboard/print-agents; choose counter binding or store-wide. The plaintext is returned only once, so store it securely right away.
  3. In the local apps/print-agent/.env, set PRINT_AGENT_API_KEY (at least 10 characters, otherwise startup validation fails), PRINT_AGENT_CLOUD_KEY where needed, and CLOUD_API_ENDPOINT (default http://localhost:8787/api/v1; it must be set explicitly in production); start the rest from .env.example.
  4. Start it on its own with pnpm dev:print-agent. The global pnpm dev excludes it by default.
  5. Check the local health, devices and the cloud agent health, then test with a real receipt.

Direction of the two keys

  • PRINT_AGENT_API_KEY: POS / same-LAN client → local HTTP / WebSocket, required at startup.
  • PRINT_AGENT_CLOUD_KEY: local agent → cloud dispatch, issued by the back office; the agent sends it to the cloud in the X-Print-Agent-Key header, and the cloud hashes it and compares it with print_agents (those not revoked), with the restaurant and register determined by that credential. It is only the agent's own environment variable name, not a browser or staff token. When unset, it is a valid local-only mode and does not poll the cloud.

Status, retries and uncertain outcomes

Ticket status goes pending → printing → printed / failed, with cancelled in addition. The claim attempt limit is MAX_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS = 5; a ticket not reported on within 5 minutes after claiming is treated as abandoned and can be reclaimed in the next round, and a ticket still unsettled after 5 attempts is marked failed. A genuine failure is automatically returned to pending and re-queued within the 5-attempt budget, and is a terminal failed once the budget is used up; indeterminate means it may already have been printed, and the cloud settles it directly as failed without automatically reprinting (to avoid duplicates), leaving a person to decide whether to reprint manually. A single claim round drains tickets one by one, up to 20; if printing fails the round stops, to avoid burning through the whole queue with retries.

Cloud health Meaning Action
online Polled recently and at least one printer is online Still confirm paper, content and encoding.
no_printer The agent is reachable, 0 printers online Check device power, IP, TCP and the driver; do not keep reprinting.
offline Not polled beyond the health window (5 minutes, OFFLINE_AFTER_MS) Check the Node process, network, cloud URL / key.
never_seen Never polled since being issued Check whether the cloud key is enabled and the correct instance is running.

Ticket content

A customer receipt contains restaurant details, payment and totals; invoice-related text is printed only when real invoice data exists. The kitchen ticket uses a separate layout: order number, table / seat, items, options, add-ons and notes, with no prices, cashier or thank-you line. The cashier's name is saved as a snapshot when the ticket is created, and a reprint does not change it to the person reprinting. Internal notes go only on the kitchen ticket.

Physical device acceptance

A successful TCP send only proves the bytes were handed to the socket; it does not prove paper came out, the cutter works or paper is loaded. For each actual model, record the brand, model, firmware, code page and command mode, print text such as "Fried rice / no spice / add egg / Lin Cashier", and check the quantity, table number, line wrapping, Chinese characters and paper cut. PRINTER_ENCODING=utf8|big5|gbk applies to all printers on the same agent; Big5 / GBK and the model's FS commands still need to be checked on a real device.

Troubleshooting

  1. First tell apart: receipts not generated, pending not claimed, printing not acknowledged, failed, or printed but no paper came out.
  2. Check whether the cloud credential binding matches the ticket's registerId, especially NULL kitchen tickets.
  3. Check the local health, whether the printer is reachable, and the last error.
  4. When unsure whether it was printed, check on site first; a manual reprint goes back to pending and may print another copy.
  5. Revoke a lost credential and issue a new one, and do not write the key into a ticket.

Part 11 · Onboarding App (Store Applications)

From public application and platform review to the Shop Owner setting a password and opening the store for the first time.

The applicant's pages

/ is the introduction entry, /apply is where the application is filled in, /success shows the success information, and /status/:applicationId checks progress. This app does not need an existing staff account; the data goes to management-api, not the main API.

Application steps

  1. Fill in the store name, contact person, email, phone, country / region and address; where a market applies, choose the market and add required information such as coordinates.
  2. Check the data and the application conditions, then submit. Public applications are IP rate limited: at most 5 applications per IP per hour (OnboardingService APPLICATION_RATE_LIMIT); on an error, correct it as prompted and do not repeatedly send duplicate data.
  3. After success, keep the applicationId and the lookup link. The link fragment / secret is the lookup credential, so you cannot just record the applicationId.
  4. Check the status such as submitted / provisioning / completed / rejected; if rejected, read the reason.
  5. After approval, you receive a set-password link (valid for 24 hours), or the platform delivers it manually. Open it on Admin Dashboard's reset-password page, set the password yourself, then sign in.

Where platform review happens

Platform Admins review in Admin Dashboard at /dashboard/platform/onboarding. The front end first exchanges a role 0 staff token for a management token, then calls the management API. Management Portal provides no application review entry point.

What the system creates after approval

Application submittedApprove → provisioningControl-plane tenant / subscriptionPlatform restaurant / Shop Owner / subscriptionOne-time set-password linkcompleted + delivery record

Both approval and rejection can only be made from the submitted status: rejection writes rejectionReason and rejectedAtMs; approving an already completed application is idempotent and directly returns the existing result, and other statuses return "Cannot approve application with status". There is no cross-database transaction between the two D1 databases; a failed approval recovers through reverse-order compensation, not a single SQL transaction. A new store may start with isAvailable=false, so that the Shop Owner completes the menu, opening hours and tables before taking orders. If a market is chosen, what is created is a pending market join request, not automatically a stall that can check out.

Credentials and emails

The initial password is an unusable random password; the Shop Owner must set a password using the one-time link. The link is valid for 24 hours, and when expired / lost the administrator regenerates it, and the new link invalidates the old token. The production configuration has ONBOARDING_EMAIL_ENABLED="true" and a Cloudflare Email binding; when disabled or sending fails, it must be delivered manually. sent means the provider accepted it, not that it reached the inbox.

The other direct store-creation entry

The platform can create a store / create an Owner and set the password on their behalf from /dashboard/account-management. The main API must call the management API through the MANAGEMENT_API service binding, and INTERNAL_API_TOKEN on both sides must be the same. When this path fails, newly created resources may be disabled; do not hand over the account just because the front end's create request was once sent.

Troubleshooting when stuck

Symptom What to check
Application lookup 401 Whether the application secret / X-Onboarding-Secret is complete; when the link fragment is not sent to the server, the front end forwards it as a header. Checking status without the secret returns 401 APPLICATION_SECRET_REQUIRED.
Shop Owner cannot sign in after approval Set the password first; username is not necessarily equal to the email; user / sessions and the restaurant status.
Approval failed: Unsupported onboarding country / PLAN_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION The applied country is not in the supported list, or the paid plan tier is not allowed by that country's plans.allowed_tiers policy (trial is not subject to this); change the application data or adjust the region policy and retry. When the region policy cannot be read, it returns 503 POLICY_UNAVAILABLE.
The administrator review page cannot load role 0, auth/exchange, API and management JWT settings, PLATFORM_DB.
provisioning / approval failed The two migrations, bindings and compensation records; re-read the application status before deciding to retry.
No email received Delivery record, the email switch, sender / binding and the inbox; protect the token during manual delivery.
The restaurant is not in the market or cannot take orders Market join review, the restaurant's isAvailable, menu and opening settings.

Acceptance should include normal approval, rejection reason, repeated approval, provisioning failure compensation, resending an expired link, real email delivery and the Shop Owner's first trial order.

Part 12 · Management Portal (Platform Control Plane)

Manages tenants and platform resources; separate from the store back office and from customer identity.

Page map

Path Purpose Operating notes
/login Obtain a management session with a platform admin identity Exchange using a valid role 0 staff token, not a Shop Owner account.
/ Platform overview Check the data source and time.
/tenants, /tenants/:id Tenants and resources tenantId is not restaurantId; create, modify and terminate (soft delete) have different effects.
/licenses License lookup, generation, renewal / upgrade Different from the shop subscription module.
/deployments Deploy / update / history There are currently contract and failure-count gaps, see below.
/health Tenant health and alerts Confirm HTTP liveness, D1 / KV dependencies and business flows separately.
/markets Control-plane markets Do not mix with the main API's admin markets endpoints.
/policies Region policy Country modules and payment policy can be an upper limit beyond the plan.

Sign-in and tenant operations

  1. First sign in with the platform account on the main API to obtain a valid staff session; then exchange for the management token.
  2. Open tenants to look up a tenant, and check the control-plane id, the linked platform restaurantId, status, license and version.
  3. Be explicit about the target before changing: changing tenant metadata, adjusting a license, changing the shop plan and disabling a restaurant are different actions.
  4. After saving, read the result back, and check the actual permissions in the corresponding store app.

The management token uses a separate issuer / audience, and its TTL is a hard-coded 1-hour constant in routes/auth.ts that cannot be changed by configuration; the portal keeps it in sessionStorage and clears it after expiry. The current management API also checks the latest platform Admin identity and the linked session, so the old documents' claim that "tokens are revoked by TTL alone" cannot be relied on.

Licenses are different from restaurant subscriptions

A license is for tenant / deployment authorization; shop_subscriptions are for the modules and quotas available to a restaurant. A license expiring, a plan changing or a module override should not be mixed into one switch. License verify is a public entry that proves itself from its payload, and other management operations need a management Bearer. The license table and the tenant columns hold redundant information, so after a change, read both sides back and check them.

Scope of terminating a tenant (soft delete)

A tenant's DELETE is actually a soft delete: TenantService.deleteTenant only sets tenants.status to terminated in MANAGEMENT_DB; it does not touch PLATFORM_DB, does not disable the restaurant or Shop Owner accounts, and does not revoke any session. It does not clear the platform restaurants, orders, payments and files. Before handling a closure or data deletion, first settle the related data, the retention policy and the account-disabling process; do not treat a single DELETE as a whole-system cleanup.

Known limitations of the deployment UI at present

The current source still shows the portal tenants store sending {tenantId, version} to deploy, while the back-end contract requires targetVersion. There are also the documented problems that the provision response type does not match the actual payload, and that VersionSync miscounts a resolved failure as completed. For this reason this handbook does not treat the Portal deploy button as a reliable production deployment flow; use the repository deployment procedure in Part 18, and first confirm the release and verification.

Markets and region policy

The platform control plane can maintain policies and markets. A module disabled at country level is an upper limit, and a single restaurant's plan and override cannot re-enable it. The main API reads the effective configuration through the policy resolver; invalid data / read failure may return 503 and should not silently let things through. When changing a policy, verify multiple restaurants in the same country, cache invalidation, different payment modes and the behavior of existing transactions.

Other platform operations work

management-api's public mounts are only /auth, /onboarding, /markets and /licenses/verify, and the rest are protected by the management Bearer; the Portal's /markets page is the operating interface for the market control plane. management-api production has one cron 30 18 * * *, which runs the onboarding audit archive; backup-scheduler additionally has an ANALYTICS binding.

The main API's Admin pages handle market stall review, cross-vendor reconciliation / refunds, the platform customer directory, shop subscriptions and announcements; Management Portal covers only the control plane. provider_split reconciliation and child_transactions reconciliation do not have the same capabilities; formal reconciliation also needs provider transaction and settlement evidence.
