Part 13 · Integrating the Main API and Management API

First pick the right service and credential, then send data according to the schema and verify the result.

Base URL

Service Local base Repository production configuration
Main API http://localhost:8787/api/v1 https://api.makanmasak.com/api/v1
Management API http://localhost:8789/api/v1 https://manage-api.makanmasak.com/api/v1
Image API http://localhost:8790 (/images, /analytics) Follows image-processor's routes configuration, and is not the main API's /api/v1.
Realtime ws://localhost:8788 wss://realtime.makanmasak.com; room paths and query tokens must follow the current client.

Some older docs use makanmakan.com or /v1, which does not match the current wrangler configuration. Follow the actual deployment and the source mounts. Local front ends usually use the relative /api/v1 through the Vite proxy; Admin also has a management API proxy, and management endpoints must not be sent to 8787.

Common principles for requests

  • Bearer:Protected endpoints carry the right kind of token, and refresh additionally needs the cookie; do not use a token from a hand-forged session.
  • CSRF:Reuse the repo client's cookie / header and Origin handling. Callbacks and guest-credential paths have precise exemptions, and you cannot exempt a whole feature yourself.
  • Identifiers:restaurantId, orderId, tenantId and tableId are of different types; new UUIDs and old integers coexist, so do not force every id to Number.
  • Amounts:The DB and most internal calculations use cents; external amount follows the route schema, so convert explicitly and carry the currency.
  • Idempotency:The order-creation clientMutationId, the payment Idempotency-Key and the webhook event key each govern different writes and should be kept until retries end.
  • Errors:Branch on HTTP status and error code, show actionable messages, and keep the request id for troubleshooting.

A runnable guest ordering example

First obtain the UUID and menuItemId from a real local restaurant / menu, then fill in the payload below. This example is a takeaway order with shop mode on and guests allowed; shopQrCode, if it comes from a scan, should carry the current value. There is no price field here, as the price is decided by the server. 

POST http://localhost:8787/api/v1/guest-orders
Content-Type: application/json
X-Guest-Device-Id: <stable identifier for this device>

{
  "restaurantId": "<actual restaurant UUID>",
  "orderType": "shop",
  "guestName": "Mr. Chen",
  "customerPhone": "<actual contact phone>",
  "clientMutationId": "<unique identifier fixed for this one submission>",
  "items": [{ "menuItemId": 123, "quantity": 1 }],
  "deliveryInfo": { "type": "takeaway" }
}

For a table order, change to orderType="table" and carry a valid tableId; for a seat order, also carry seatId. The current guest schema allows at most 20 items per order, with a quantity of at most 99 each; do not apply the larger limits of other order entry points here. After a successful response, keep the original order id and the guest token; reading / adding to / cancelling use the matching guest authorization paths.

Management token exchange example

POST http://localhost:8789/api/v1/auth/exchange
Content-Type: application/json

{ "token": "<role 0 access token obtained from a normal main API sign-in>" }

Then:
GET http://localhost:8789/api/v1/tenants
Authorization: Bearer <the management token obtained from the exchange>

The exchange checks the Admin identity and the staff session. The JWT_SECRET with which the main API / management verify an incoming token must be the same; management issuance can use a separate MANAGEMENT_JWT_SECRET. INTERNAL_API_TOKEN is a server-to-server credential and must never be handed to the front end.

Common business endpoints

Feature Full main API path Usage
Public menu GET /api/v1/menu/:restaurantId Read categories, items and options; sellable data is still checked again at order time.
Guest order POST /api/v1/guest-orders Anonymous or optional customer identity; obtain the guest token after success.
Order list / details GET /api/v1/orders, /:id Identity and the restaurant's scope; the list needs pagination handling.
Fulfillment status PUT /api/v1/orders/:id/status role, transition, claim and version checks; must not be used to mark paid.
Kitchen item PUT /api/v1/kitchen/:restaurantId/orders/:orderId/items/:itemId After an item changes, the server checks whole-order progress.
Claim an order POST /api/v1/orders/:id/delivery-claim Saves the server assignment; a repeated claim may return 409.
Payment POST /api/v1/payments, /payments/create staff auth and Idempotency-Key; the two contracts' bodies must not be mixed freely.
POS refund POST /api/v1/pos/refunds/create POS binding and submission for approval; the approve endpoint is called separately.
Issue a receipt POST /api/v1/pos/receipts/print Module / quota; writes pending, and completes only after the agent acknowledges.
Cloud printing GET /api/v1/print/jobs, POST /jobs/:receiptId/ack header X-Print-Agent-Key (the cloud compares by hash against print_agents); not a browser staff token. PRINT_AGENT_CLOUD_KEY is only the environment variable name on the print-agent side that stores this key.
Wait list /api/v1/waiting-list The public / ticket-authorized section differs from the staff calling section.
Service bookings /api/v1/service-bookings Services, slots, confirmation code, payment conditions and flags.
Group orders /api/v1/orders/group create / join / cart / lock / tracking-token / split; member authorization.
Market checkout /api/v1/market-checkouts Per-vendor child orders, coupons, payment, webhook, platform reconciliation and refunds.

Responses and errors

The general API uses {success, data} or the unified error data, but the health endpoints, Realtime, the image service and legacy routes are exceptions. Look at the actual response and the feature schema, and do not force one unwrap on every service. Typical statuses: 400 parameters, 401 identity / session, 403 permission / module, 404 not found or feature disabled, 409 resource / amount / version conflict, 429 rate limit / quota, 503 provider or dependency unavailable.

Pagination, caching and retries

The pagination in list responses must not be ignored; the first-page-only limit on the current service list and the like is also a known problem. When using a date range, confirm whether the field applied is createdAt or deliveredAt, and the restaurant's timezone. GET can be retried per policy; writes must keep an idempotency identifier; on a payment timeout, check the transaction first. Receiving a realtime event can update the cache, but after a disconnect recovers, re-read the server, and do not infer the final state yourself from the order in which events arrive.

Sources and limits of API documentation

Appendix A lists, item by item, the current mounts and the literal paths in the registered documentation, helping to locate the current handler; detailed payloads follow the validation / schema each route uses. Although the repo has OpenAPI integration code, the current app-factory does not call it, so /info listing docs does not guarantee that /docs or /openapi.json is available. Integration verification should call the actual Hono routes directly.

Part 14 · Realtime, WebSocket and Events

Room isolation and token exchange let each station see changes to the same order.

Service roles

The main API does writes and emits events; the realtime Worker takes the WebSocket and hands it to the RealtimeSession Durable Object. Rooms are located by name; the API and realtime must reference the same DO namespace / script and conventions, and the two will not interoperate merely because each creates a class of the same name.

Room Main recipients Event purpose
admin:{restaurantId} Admin Dashboard New orders, status, menu changes and so on.
kitchen:{restaurantId} Kitchen Display New orders / items / fulfillment status.
customer:{tableId} Customer table (path /customer/:tableId) Order updates for the customers at that table.
customer:order:{orderId} Customer single-order tracking (path /customer/order:{orderId}) Status updates for that order; does not broadcast the whole restaurant's private orders.
customer:{groupOrderId} Group order members (path /customer/{groupOrderId}) The room is isolated by groupOrderId; the member token scope is group-order-realtime, roomId must equal groupOrderId, and it is issued by /realtime/auth/group-token.

The realtime Worker exposes only /customer/:tableId, /admin/:restaurantId, /kitchen/:restaurantId and /health. The API's token request accepts only a roomType of admin or kitchen; the restaurant room has been removed (the old version would issue tokens and URLs for connections that were bound to 404).

Connection flow

  1. First hold a valid staff / customer / guest order identity.
  2. Request the matching room token from the main API; guests use the guest-token exchange, rather than using a guest token directly as a staff JWT.
  3. Send a WebSocket Upgrade to the correct room path on realtime. The path is /{roomType}/{roomId}, and the token is read only from the query string ?token= (jwtVerifier.extractTokenFromUrl), not from a header; the guest roomId for an order scope is order:{orderId}, the customer room token comes from /realtime/auth/guest-token, staff use /realtime/auth/token, and group orders use /realtime/auth/group-token.
  4. The DO validates the token's validity period, scope and permissions before accepting messages.
  5. On reconnect, refresh the authorization; after expiry / revocation, clear the old connection token and re-fetch the server data.

Local and production configuration

Locally, the api / realtime JWT_SECRET must be the same; when REALTIME_JWT_SECRET is set, it must also match on both sides. The front-end names REALTIME_URL / WS_BASE_URL / REALTIME_WS_URL differ by app, so do not blindly unify the variable names. Production uses wss and allowed origins, and the API needs the REALTIME_SESSION binding.

Two common misjudgments

  • API succeeded but no notification:The DB state may already be written, and a broadcast failure does not roll it back automatically; re-fetch the details, and check the DO binding, scope and room name.
  • An SSE connection means everything updates:The kitchen SSE currently only sends heartbeats, and order events go over WebSocket; ServiceView still polls every 15 seconds. Different apps cannot use one green light to prove the whole chain.

Rate limiting and recoverability

WebSocket upgrade has realtime rate limiting; a failure of the rate-limit dependency may return 503. A network reconnect does not guarantee that all lost events are replayed. Clients recover using the current resource state, and should not treat event history as a complete audit. Cross-device verification should go from real browser operations to the API, the DO, another station and the customer page, and not substitute unit-mocked events.

Part 15 · Image Processor (Image Service)

Image content, visibility, metadata and menu binding are a separate service path.

What it is responsible for

A standalone Worker handles upload, storage and image metadata, variants / processing jobs, viewing and statistics. The request entry points are /images and /analytics, and the main API's /api/v1 must not be prepended. It validates files by type and size, and uses the image DB, R2 and cache; Cloudflare Images-related capabilities need provider configuration.

Shop Owner upload and binding

  1. In the back-office menu / restaurant image field, choose a file; check the content, format and size.
  2. The front end sends the file to the image service, carrying the correct staff identity and restaurant owner information.
  3. After a successful upload, obtain the image identifier and usable URL / variant, then associate it with the menu / restaurant data.
  4. After saving, view it from the customer side. If the metadata exists but the image is broken, check R2 / Images / variant and the public access rules separately.
  5. Before replacing or deleting, confirm which menus / restaurants still reference it; do not assume references are cleared just because the image object was deleted.

Main API categories

Service path Purpose
POST /images/upload Validate and upload an image; role 0 / 1 / 2.
GET / PUT / DELETE /images/:id GET is optional auth (publicly viewable images can be read without signing in); PUT / DELETE role 0 / 1 / 2.
GET /images List and filter; sign-in required.
GET /images/:id/view, /:imageId/:variant Serves image viewing / variants per route; /:id/view is optional auth, and /:imageId/:variant does not require sign-in.
POST /images/:id/process, GET /images/jobs/:jobId Process requests role 0 / 1 / 2; job status requires sign-in.
POST /images/bulk Bulk operations; role 0 / 1 only.
/analytics/* Storage, usage and performance analytics.
/health, /info Dependency health and service metadata.

Configuration and troubleshooting

Confirm Admin's VITE_IMAGE_API_URL, the service CORS, the staff verification secret, the image DB, IMAGE_CACHE, IMAGES_BUCKET and the Images provider. Limits (wrangler.toml): the production URL is images.makanmasak.com; MAX_IMAGE_SIZE_MB 10 (single file), MAX_UPLOAD_REQUEST_SIZE_MB 12 (the whole upload request), MAX_UPLOADS_PER_MINUTE 20, MAX_TRANSFORMS_PER_MINUTE 100; ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES are image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp and image/gif, and any other MIME is rejected. The restaurant / owner UUID format must agree with the generation strategy. The image health probe performs a KV write, unlike the main API's cheap read-only health, so do not blindly call it at high frequency.

Acceptance

Test a valid image, an oversized image, a wrong MIME, another restaurant's owner, public versus private visibility, customer refresh after changing an image, deleting an image that is still referenced, an unavailable provider and a processing failure. The image README keeps old npm steps; this repo uses only pnpm and the current wrangler configuration.

Part 16 · Plans, Modules, Quotas and Region Policy

A feature existing, the plan allowing it, the region allowing it and the provider being connected are four different things.

The 14 current modules

Group Modules Functions
Core menu_management, table_management, online_ordering Menu, tables, orders.
Pro pos, kitchen_display, receipt_printing, coupons, reservations, analytics Cashiering, kitchen, printing, coupons, reservations / wait list, analytics.
Enterprise ai_analytics, platform_integration, loyalty, inventory, staff_management AI, delivery integration, loyalty, ingredients / recipes, staffing.

Plan defaults and overrides

basic contains the 3 core modules; pro contains core + 6 pro; enterprise and trial contain all 14. The trial length is defined by the shared plan-mapping and is currently 180 days. In the current moduleGate, trial expiry is a reminder and does not block directly; do not follow the old flow saying "expiry is always 403". A disabled isActive is still rejected, and after that a module override takes priority over the plan default; role 0 bypasses the module gate. Region policy is still the upper limit on the effective modules of an ordinary restaurant.

module_overrides is a sparse overlay: true force-enables, false force-disables, and no key falls back to the plan default. Changing the plan clears the overrides, so after an upgrade / downgrade, re-check exceptional authorizations. An API boolean patch and deleting an override key have different semantics, and false must not be treated as returning to the default.

Modules, quotas and feature flags

Control Question it answers Typical result
moduleGate Is this restaurant entitled to use POS / kitchen / staffing? 403 MODULE_NOT_ENABLED / SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND.
region policy Does this country allow a given module or payment strategy? 403 MODULE_NOT_AVAILABLE_IN_REGION, or 503 when the policy cannot be read.
quota Use is allowed, but how much has been used this cycle? In enforce mode, 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED.
feature adoption flag Is a capability that is not formally enabled open platform-wide? When off, the route returns 404 and the UI should hide or explain it.
provider readiness The feature is on, but is there a usable external provider? A missing payment / SMS / Email provider may give 409 / 503 and does not manufacture a success result.

Environment differences

The quota middleware defaults to disabled when no value is set; the current production in apps/api/wrangler.toml explicitly sets QUOTA_ENFORCEMENT_MODE="enforce". The default behavior must not be taken directly as production behavior. The subscription KV cache is 300 seconds; changes made through the management API usually invalidate it, while direct SQL changes may keep the old result until the TTL expires or it is invalidated manually.

Flags that need special confirmation

Feature Flag Default when unset Additional prerequisites
Stored-value credits STORED_VALUE_CREDITS_ENABLED Off Top-up / deduction / refund policy, ledger consistency and real transaction acceptance.
Tenant backups TENANT_BACKUPS_ENABLED Off Integration of the scheduler with the feature service path, scheduling, and real restore acceptance.
Market checkout MARKET_CHECKOUTS_ENABLED On Market members / production data, provider, callbacks and per-vendor settlement.
Staff / general push WEB_PUSH_ENABLED On sender / deliverer and valid VAPID; a route being open is not the same as delivered.
Customer push CUSTOMER_WEB_PUSH_ENABLED Off Server VAPID, front-end public key, subscription and background delivery.

The disabledFeatures of GET /info shares its declaration with the route gate and is the starting point for checking feature visibility; deployment overrides and providers still need to be checked. The older 2026-10-04 verification confirmed that some production features are off, and this time that old snapshot is not promoted into a new remote measurement.

Country, currency and time zone

A restaurant stores its country, currency and time zone, and onboarding creates defaults by country. Cross-restaurant finance is grouped by currency; business hours and daily close are interpreted in the restaurant's timezone. A policy misconfiguration should be rejected explicitly. Multiple restaurants with different currencies, late-night trading across days, or a browser and restaurant in different time zones are boundaries that must be verified.

Part 17 · Data Model, Shared Packages and Migrations

Platform data, control-plane data, short-lived credentials and files live in different resources.

Core data map

Domain Main data What the connection means
Restaurants and staff restaurants, users, sessions, shop_subscriptions Staff belong to a restaurant; the session is part of identity; the subscription grants modules.
Customers and member relationships customers, customer_auth_identities, restaurant_customers Platform-wide customers are separate from a restaurant's member relationship.
Menu categories, menu_items, option_groups and choices / bindings Customer options and prices come from the catalog; menu changes affect new orders.
Orders orders, order_items One order and its line items; version, time, payment, customer and restaurant scope.
Tables and ticket numbers tables, seats, waiting_list, reservations Real seats and wait list / reservation resources; different state machines.
Services restaurant_service_items, service_bookings and so on Service data, slot capacity, confirmation code, deposit and reminders.
Payments and POS payment_transactions, cash_registers, cash_shifts, cash_movements, refunds, receipts Transactions, cash drawer, refunds, print-pending snapshots; follow the actual table names in each schema.
Printing print_agents, receipts credentials are defined by migration; paired by restaurant + register / null.
Group orders and markets group_orders, group_cart_items, markets, memberships, market_checkout_* Same-restaurant multi-person one master; cross-vendor multiple children.
Staffing employee_schedules, shift_templates, leave_*, schedule_swap_requests and so on Shifts, availability, leave and requests; not customers.
Quota and analytics usage_events, usage_meters, usage_meter_buckets, cycle_snapshots Usage metering and cycle statistics; do not replace the transaction ledger.
Control plane tenants, licenses, onboarding_applications, deployment / audit data Lives in MANAGEMENT_DB; connects to platform restaurants through linking fields.

The various Cloudflare storage types

  • D1:Persists domain data and transactions. There are two databases, platform and control plane, and the image service has its own DB; do not blur bindings with "everything is D1".
  • KV:Cache, guest credentials / active locks, subscriptions, blocklists and so on; it has a TTL and is not a permanent source for every business.
  • R2:Images / bundles / backup or audit archive objects; a D1 restore does not roll R2 back with it.
  • Durable Object:Real-time rooms; not the financial ledger.
  • Queue:Search index sync fan-out; not the same concept as the in-store paper ticket or wait list queue.

Nine shared workspaces

Package Responsibility Impact of changes
@makanmasak/shared-types Roles, order statuses, API / domain types Front-end and back-end contract and state machines.
@makanmasak/database Drizzle schema, D1 services, domain persistence Data, transactions, amounts, permission boundaries.
@makanmasak/shared Shared UI / resources and some utilities Multiple Vue apps.
@makanmasak/i18n (nested workspace) Language resources in packages/shared/src/i18n User-facing copy and locale loading.
@makanmasak/utils Shared general utilities, error / recovery and so on Called from many places; check callers before changing.
@makanmasak/auth-client Front-end authentication and API client Bearer, cookie / refresh, error handling.
@makanmasak/ai-analytics AI and product analytics Provider and data analysis.
@makanmasak/queue-core Queue foundation and printing core / drivers Local printing, commands and queues.
@makanmasak/queue-service Queue service layer Confirm by the actual place of use; do not confuse it with Cloudflare Queues.

Schema and SQL are not the same thing

The Drizzle schema is the source of tables and columns; triggers, partial indexes, CHECK and STRICT are also in the migration SQL. Appendix B lists the tables / columns in the schema to help with lookup, and does not mean the live database and the fresh baseline are identical. uuid v7 is the direction for new domains, but old integer ids still exist; timestamp_ms uses INTEGER milliseconds; integer cents protect monetary precision.

The two actual migration tracks

Track Target Binding / command
packages/database/migrations_fresh/ Platform DB api DB, realtime platform DB, management PLATFORM_DB; pnpm db:migrate:local:api / db:migrate:prod.
apps/management-api/migrations/ Control-plane DB management MANAGEMENT_DB; pnpm db:migrate:local:mgmt / db:migrate:prod:mgmt.
packages/database/migrations/, migrations_v2/ Historical directories No wrangler migrations_dir points at them; do not write into them expecting automatic deployment.

The correct order for adding / changing data

  1. First read the Database section of CLAUDE, and confirm the binding, track, latest sequence number and production lineage.
  2. Change the schema and export it, and hand-write the corresponding SQL; new tables and the temporary table of a recreate need STRICT.
  3. For a retryable nullable key use a DB-level partial unique, use INTEGER ms for timestamps, and put secrets only in encrypted payloads.
  4. Register / document the change per dual-track, apply the local migration and verify real D1 behavior.
  5. Verify the new database and the existing database separately; an existing ledger row in the database cannot prove the schema is the same as the fresh baseline.
  6. A manual production recreate must first obtain a schema copy, replay it and check the end state; the operator carries it out under the formal runbook.

pnpm db:generate is not this repo's default migration flow. The production FTS5 shape breaks the old export flow; and the fresh baseline must not be replayed onto the existing production database. Migrations, restores and schema differences should all follow CLAUDE and the runbooks.

D1 atomicity

D1 has no arbitrarily interactive transaction; related operations use batch, conditional UPDATE, version CAS and failure compensation. Across databases or across vendors there is no single huge transaction wrapping everything. A successful business response must match the durable write; the return of a pending id alone cannot prove the work has been saved.

Part 18 · Local Development, Testing and Deployment

Use the existing workspace commands to build a reproducible environment, and get the whole flow working end to end locally first.

Development prerequisites

Node minimum 22.18, and the repo pins pnpm 12.3.4; packageManager is the authoritative version, and the looser engines does not mean an older pnpm is acceptable. Install only with pnpm. pnpm settings live in pnpm-workspace.yaml; do not move overrides or allowBuilds back to places that are no longer read.

Initialization

pnpm install
cp apps/api/.dev.vars.example apps/api/.dev.vars
cp apps/management-api/.dev.vars.example apps/management-api/.dev.vars
cp apps/realtime/.dev.vars.example apps/realtime/.dev.vars

# Edit the gitignored files above and put in local-only random secrets
pnpm db:migrate:local
pnpm db:seed:local
pnpm dev

Do not overwrite personal configuration that already exists; the cp above is for when the local files have not been created yet. Use pnpm exec wrangler login for Cloudflare sign-in when you need to access remote resources. Local migrations use the shared ./.wrangler/shared-state, and api and management must read the same persist directory; you cannot each build an isolated local DB and then expect onboarding to find the same restaurant.

Secret and URL configuration

Setting Purpose Consistency
JWT_SECRET staff / room and incoming management exchange verification api, realtime and management incoming verification must match, at least 32 characters.
INTERNAL_API_TOKEN api→management internal service authentication Identical on both sides, never sent to the front end.
QR_SIGNING_KEY Table / seat QR signing A locally generated secure random value; creating / rotating QR fails when it is missing.
ENCRYPTION_KEY Third-party credentials and encrypted data For the features that need it; production must store it securely, and if lost it cannot be recovered.
MANAGEMENT_JWT_SECRET Tokens issued by management itself Optional separate secret; verification and issuance are the same.
REALTIME_JWT_SECRET Optional guest room issuance When set, api and realtime match.
VITE_API_BASE_URL and so on Front-end build-time URL / flags VITE values are publicly visible; put no secrets in them.
CLIENT_BASE_URL / ADMIN_APP_URL / ONBOARDING_APP_URL Landing points for QR / verification / set-password / application links Must point to the app that actually has the corresponding route, and not rely on the ordering of the CORS list.

Starting a single service

pnpm dev:api
pnpm dev:customer
pnpm dev:admin
pnpm dev:kitchen
pnpm dev:management:all
pnpm dev:print-agent

# Apps without a shortcut command can use a workspace filter
pnpm --filter ./apps/onboarding-app dev
pnpm --filter @makanmasak/realtime dev

customer / admin / kitchen have committed .env.development and example files, and personal overrides use .env.development.local. management-portal and onboarding follow the existing defaults / local configuration. The Vite proxy lets the front end work with the local API; production does not automatically use the development proxy, and the build configuration must point at the deployment URL.

Testing and inner-loop checks

Command Purpose
pnpm verify Inner loop of typecheck, lint and tests for the affected workspaces.
pnpm verify:push The full local pre-push gate; includes format, guards, root/package and real integration.
pnpm test Vitest workspace.
pnpm test:real-integration Real-service integration runner; confirm the specific filter and environment.
pnpm test:e2e Playwright browser; needs an actual stack and the specified projects.
pnpm build Builds all workspaces; a successful static build does not mean external providers are available.
pnpm lint:fix The repo's pre-commit format / lint fix; commit only intended changes.
pnpm check:design-palette / check:docs-drift UI palette / consistency of generated blocks in managed documents.

Testing is layered as unit, real D1, browser, production and hardware. An expected fail / skip cannot count as that path being done; when the E2E stack is not up, use strict mode, and do not treat skipping as passing. Real staff tests must obtain tokens from a normal login or a shared fixture that creates a valid session; do not weaken authentication to make tests pass.

Deployment order and verification

  1. Record the target SHA, change scope, apps / Workers, schema, flags, providers and the rollback plan.
  2. Run the necessary checks and the affected tests; complete the build and review the diff.
  3. When there is SQL, first verify the track and compatibility with the existing database; the platform and control-plane deployment commands are separate.
  4. Schedule compatible releases of API / realtime / management / front end; a named env binding does not automatically inherit top-level, so confirm the production configuration item by item.
  5. When deployment is needed, use the repo's pnpm deploy:prod or the corresponding workspace deploy:prod; the command changes the production environment and is run only by an authorized release process.
  6. After release, check /info, dependency health, a real QR, sign-in, ordering, kitchen, service, cash payment and receipt; verify providers and hardware separately.
  7. Record the deploy id / version, time and result, and hand them over to operations.

CI / local automation must not add destructive D1 delete / time-travel restore / Worker delete commands. Production migrations, rollback and disaster recovery follow the runbooks; writing this handbook did not deploy anything or modify production data.

Principles for changing shared code

First check all callers before changing a shared service / type. The state machine and role table come from shared-types; guard the server contract for amounts and authentication first; do not copy a helper that another app already has. New UI follows DESIGN and design-tokens; new behavior updates meaningful tests. When related changes are complete, make an atomic Conventional Commit, and do not push without explicit instruction.

Part 19 · Cross-App Troubleshooting and Handover

First locate the real state at which layer, then decide whether to retry, fix configuration or handle manually.

General troubleshooting order

  1. Define the scenario:Which restaurant, which app, which role, which order number / checkout / ticket number, and the time of occurrence and time zone.
  2. Look at the network:The actual request URL, method, HTTP status, error code and request id; do not just copy the toast.
  3. Check identity:Whether the staff / customer / guest / management / room token was chosen correctly, and whether the session is active.
  4. Check scope:Whether the restaurant / tenant / table / order are in the same resource chain.
  5. Check availability:The restaurant can take orders, items are sellable, module, region policy, flag, quota, provider.
  6. Read the server:Re-read the single resource, transaction, refund, receipt or application, and confirm whether it has been written.
  7. Check channels and caches:Look at REST, KV, WebSocket, SSE, polling and the offline queue separately.
  8. Choose recovery:Supply data / sign in again / retry with the original key / resync / manual check; do not mask a failure by changing DB state directly.

Symptom lookup table

Symptom Possible cause Safe next step
Customer's order submission timed out, but the restaurant already has the order response / network lost; the DB already succeeded Look up the original order by clientMutationId / order number, keeping the original identifier key.
Customer can see the menu but cannot order Opening hours, guest switch, shop mode, inventory, minimum spend, quota Check the error code and refresh the cart; a public GET does not mean writes are open.
Shop Owner has the page but gets 403 module / region / scope; or session permissions changed Check the subscription and identity, and do not use a role 0 bypass as acceptance.
A correctly signed JWT still gets 401 active session missing / revoked, tokenVersion / claim drift Sign in again normally; fix the test fixture rather than loosening auth.
Kitchen sees only old orders pending not confirmed, WebSocket / cache out of sync Check the API queue and parent status, the room binding; then refresh from the server.
All dishes ready but the whole order does not change Current server chain fault, old deployment or sync failure Check the KitchenService response and version, and do not assume the old design that needs a manual push again.
Service's numbers for today are wrong Only queries delivered, createdAt date, first page Check orders across days and those paid afterwards; do not treat it as complete statistics for now.
Card / wallet looks successful, the order is not settled callback signature not verified / provider has not credited / uncertain transaction Check the transaction and provider result, and avoid charging again with a new key.
Refund processing Needs approval, provider result undecided Ask the Owner / Admin to approve and check the real money returned.
Ticket stuck in pending Agent cloud key / register/null binding, no printer Look at the agent and the local device, and do not change pending to printed.
TCP succeeded but no paper came out Paper, cutter, command / encoding mismatch Check the real machine on site; printed is a transport report, not a paper sensor.
Onboarding approved but no email Email delivery failed / disabled / filtered Check the delivery record, deliver safely by hand or resend the link.
Just changed a module and still rejected KV not invalidated, region policy still off Re-read through the management API normally; check the cache and the effective region configuration.
Management deployment 400 version / targetVersion contract gap Handle per the known limitations, and do not treat pressing deploy repeatedly as a retry.
Health 200 but orders unavailable liveness differs from dependency / business Check dependency health and actually walk the original path.

Minimum content of a support ticket

Provide the app and page route, restaurant / order number, role, time of occurrence and time zone, steps taken, expected versus actual, HTTP / code / request id, and whether it is reproducible. For payment problems add the transaction / refund identifier and idempotency key identifier; for printing problems add the receipt and agent identifiers. Do not paste a full JWT, guest token, cookie, application secret, cloud key or sensitive payment content.

Handover check

When told "it is fixed", ask for the corresponding version / environment, a verification command that can be rerun, the original failing scenario and the result. A unit test only proves the branch under test; local D1 is not remote Cloudflare; a fake TCP is not a physical printer; provider accepted is not the inbox / credited. Decide whether the handover is complete by the real user path.

Part 20 · Monitoring, Backup, Recovery and Known Limitations

System disaster recovery and the tenant backup feature are different things; an unscheduled job must not be treated as a safety net.

Different purposes of the health endpoints

Main API endpoint What it checks How to use it
GET /info Static metadata and feature visibility; does not probe D1 / KV Starting point for liveness and deployment configuration.
GET /api/v1/monitoring/health D1 and read-only KV + monitoring signals Look at overall/components; not the general success/data envelope.
GET /api/v1/system/health Read-only dependency probes, D1 service region and so on Can be used as a cheap dependency check.
GET /api/v1/system/health?deep=1 Includes the KV write path and uptime evidence Needs a Bearer; not for high-frequency public polling.
/api/v1/system/health/live, ready, uptime Dedicated probes / evidence Need a Bearer; external monitors must support tokens.

When configuring monitoring, keep HTTP liveness, dependencies, business and actual notification separate. An isolate counter with no traffic does not prove D1 is healthy; the main monitoring path also uses real probes. Aggregate statistics, alert thresholds and product SLOs are not the same number.

Cron and background tasks

The api entry has token / log cleanup, usage rollup, forecast warm-up, payment reconciliation, group order expiry, overdue order alerts and so on, run according to the wrangler crons and cronMatches; the Queue consumer handles search fan-out, with retry on failure. management production additionally has an onboarding audit archive task. backup-scheduler is a separate Worker configuration, currently crons=[], so it cannot be said that a full set of tenant backups runs automatically every day.

backup-scheduler app quick reference

Item Details
What it is A Worker shell with only wrangler.toml, package.json and turbo.json. main points at apps/api/src/workers/backup-scheduler.ts, so changing the backup scheduling logic means going to the api directory, not this folder.
Entry form It handles only the scheduled event; there is no HTTP route, no UI, no local port and no /info, so a health endpoint cannot be used to confirm whether it is running. To see its execution you can only look at the Worker log and Analytics.
Current schedule [triggers] crons = [], deliberately left empty. The reason is recorded in wrangler.toml: backup is a per-restaurant feature, and the schedule processes only the backup_configurations entries with schedule_enabled = true; production currently has none, so the original health check every 5 minutes amounted to 8,640 idle runs a month. When restoring it, only an empty array clears the old trigger at deployment; deleting the whole block leaves the old trigger running.
The four retained scheduling intents */5 * * * * health check and monitoring; 0 */6 * * * handles each restaurant's scheduled backups; 0 2 * * * daily cleanup and maintenance; 0 0 * * SUN weekly report and alerts. Triggers are matched with cronMatches, and a cron it does not recognize is only logged and does nothing. All four are currently comments and will not run.
Binding DB (D1; dev is makanmakan-local, production is makanmasak-prod), BACKUP_KV, BACKUP_STORAGE (R2; production is makanmasak-backups-prod), ANALYTICS. Environment names: default, development, production (Worker name makanmasak-backup-scheduler-prod).
Commands pnpm --filter @makanmasak/backup-scheduler build and build:prod only do wrangler deploy --dry-run; its test is this dry-run build, while typecheck / lint are forwarded to the api package. Only deploy:prod actually deploys. pnpm check:workers builds it as well.
What it is not It is not the platform's disaster recovery. Platform recovery relies on D1 Time Travel (see "Platform recovery procedure" below), unrelated to this Worker, and whether it has a schedule does not affect Time Travel.
Prerequisites to enable At least one tenant has actually turned on a backup setting; TENANT_BACKUPS_ENABLED has been decided; the scheduler / BackupService inconsistencies listed in the next section are fixed; backup → restore has been run in an isolated environment; then move the cron you need from the comments back into crons and deploy.

Current limitations of tenant backup

TENANT_BACKUPS_ENABLED is off by default. The scheduler entry is at apps/api/src/workers/backup-scheduler.ts, and it currently imports the legacy BackupService; recent verification recorded gaps such as its pending acknowledgment not actually writing backup_records and the service and table names being inconsistent. The feature BackupService has a different write / encrypt / checksum path, and a passing test on it cannot replace scheduler acceptance. First fix the consistency and test backup→restore in isolation, then talk about enabling the schedule.

Platform recovery procedure

The repo's backup-restore-runbook treats D1 Time Travel as the platform recovery mechanism and records the isolated drill of 2026-07-30. The retention period and the current live configuration must be reconfirmed during an incident, and cannot rely only on the historical 30-day value. Production has two databases, platform and management, and an incident may span both; one restore only rolls back the target D1, not KV, R2 and Queue.

  1. Freeze further deployments and necessary writes, and judge whether the incident involves an app, Worker, D1, secret or provider.
  2. Save the current bookmarks of the two affected databases, the bad version / time and forensic data.
  3. Preview the bookmark corresponding to the target time, and confirm the normal writes that would be lost.
  4. Through the formal recovery runbook, the operator performs the restore in an interactive environment, and saves the undo bookmark immediately.
  5. Verify key rows, foreign keys, FTS queries and triggers, then deal with the KV cache, R2 references and Queue leftovers.
  6. Walk through sign-in, orders, payments and the control-plane links again, record the results and reopen writes.

This handbook does not attach a destructive recovery script that could be run by mistake. Wrangler may auto-confirm in a non-interactive environment; the repo already has a guard that forbids automated destructive commands. Production FTS5 makes the usual D1 export flow unusable, so forensics and recovery should follow the current runbook.

Release rollback

Worker rollback, Pages rollback, schema restore and secret restore are different. First capture the deployment id and the earliest bad time, and use the rollback-runbook to recover the affected layer; a code rollback does not automatically undo a D1 migration. The standard for a completed rollback is that the broken user path is restored, not just /info returning 200.

Go-live capabilities and acceptance prerequisites

Capability Scope this handbook can confirm Still to be done
Basic ordering, kitchen, cash POS Current source code and recent local / regression data The live store's actual QR, roles, the full chain, and cross-day / offline verification.
OAuth / Email / SMS Routes and configurable providers exist Production credentials, callbacks, real delivery / recovery.
Market online payment, per-vendor split Provider and fail-closed paths and local control-boundary tests Payment provider adapter, callback signature verification, refund crediting and settlement.
Stored value / customer Push Flags default to off; the UI and routes must be consistent Product decision to enable, credentials, public key, ledger / background notification acceptance.
Physical printing Real TCP transport, a separate kitchen layout and encoding capability Acceptance on each actual model for Chinese text, paper, cutter, and disconnect / uncertain reprint.
Portal deployment / batch update Still has the version contract and returned failure counting gaps Fix the contract and verify real Cloudflare deployment / rollback.
Tenant automatic backup Flag off, crons empty; legacy path gaps Unify the service and persistence contract, real backup restore and scheduling.
Durable audit of all business actions Some operations have audits, which cannot prove every mutation is fully recorded A clear coverage table of key actions and per-entry persistence.

Decisions the operator needs to make

For each extended capability, list the owner, enable / not enable / defer, the provider and production data, the acceptance evidence and the conditions for restarting. Turning off an unused capability is a legitimate product scope; external training and sales must not promise payments, push, independent deployment or hardware support that has not been verified.

Part 21 · Glossary, Data Identifiers and Handbook Maintenance

Use the same vocabulary to discuss flows, avoiding confusion from queues, tokens or management pages that share a name.

Term Meaning
Restaurant The operating restaurant scope; menus, tables, staff and orders belong to it.
Tenant A control-plane management unit linked to a restaurant; not a customer account.
Staff / Customer Two identities: staff users and canonical customers.
Guest Token The permission for a single anonymous order; not a public QR.
Shop QR / Table QR / Seat QR A public restaurant identifier; table / seat codes carry a signature and version check.
Order ID / Order Number Internal primary key / on-site readable order number; should not be confused with a table number.
Master / Child Order The merged group order / the per-vendor child orders a market creates.
Fulfillment / Payment Two status axes: food fulfillment / money transactions.
Cents / Currency Integer amount scale / currency; each API's amount unit follows its schema.
Module Override / Feature Flag A restaurant's module override / platform-wide feature availability.
Queue May be the wait list compatibility entry, a Cloudflare search queue or the local print queue; make clear which.
Claim / Ack Taking a task / reporting the observed result; claiming does not mean completion.
SSE / WebSocket One-way EventSource stream / two-way room connection; the kitchen uses them for different purposes.
Binding A runtime resource handle through which a Worker accesses D1, KV, R2, a DO or a service.
STRICT / Partial Unique / CAS SQLite type constraint / conditional unique index / update conditioned on the current state or version.
Time Travel / Tenant Backup Platform D1 historical restore / a tenant product feature; check enablement and evidence separately.

Handbook maintenance process

  1. When changing app routes, permissions, statuses, features, providers or migrations, update the corresponding main chapter; the appendix source inventory must also be rebuilt. The route literal index is rescanned from each app's source code under the scanning rules above and compared file by file (the counts of entries and files must match the headings and this paragraph).
  2. Record the verification date, SHA and environment, and label the three kinds of evidence: "source code", "configuration" and "production measurement".
  3. Do not restate defects from historical QA as today's facts, and do not upgrade a mock / test pass into hardware or remote provider acceptance.
  4. Maintain contents anchors and source links, format the HTML; confirm offline, desktop / mobile and print.
  5. After completion, commit the related files for the owner to audit; changes to this handbook do not automatically trigger push / deploy.

Method and scope of this inventory

After updating, run pnpm exec node scripts/check-system-handbook.cjs, which checks chapters, anchors, source files, search, deep links and print expand / restore. Then confirm the mobile and desktop layout in a browser; this document check does not replace each app's functional tests.

Code structure used codebase-memory (Tier 2) and reading the source back; configuration / literal routes / non-code documents were read directly. The evidence paths have coverage checks, and a best-effort graph index cannot prove there are no omissions at all. The main text cross-checks the current router, auth, orders, KitchenService, PaymentService, moduleGate, feature-adoption and wrangler; recent investigations provide dated verification limits.

This handbook covers the responsibilities, entry points, operations, dependencies, errors and technical seams of all 11 apps / services; it is not a replacement for an online Swagger of every field. The appendices give the current literal registrations and schema fields, while payload rules, SQL-only constraints and the actual deployment still defer to the corresponding source / migration / runbook as authoritative.

下表列的是「檔案內的路由路徑」，不是自動組合完成的對外URL。組完整URL時需向上核對本檔router如何被掛載：例如orders/routes的 /:id/status 配主掛載 /orders 得到 /api/v1/orders/:id/status。POS子router、auth、同prefix多router要再查其內部route掛載；是否public、deprecated、flag或module關閉則由middleware與handler決定。

此索引共92個檔案、757筆，掃描範圍為 apps/api/src、apps/management-api/src、apps/realtime/src、apps/image-processor/src、apps/print-agent/src 內所有非測試.ts，收錄任何Hono／Express receiver（app、authRoutes、adminRoutes、print-agent的router等）上以字串／template literal寫成、且以 / 開頭的 get／post／put／patch／delete 註冊（含跨行寫法）；略過測試檔、註解、非literal／動態建路徑，以及use／all／route 等非HTTP-method註冊。同一路徑不同method分列。apps/api/src/openapi/integration.ts 的 /docs、/openapi.json 因 integrateOpenAPI 目前沒有被任何程式掛載，未列入；apps/print-agent 的11筆為Express路由，檔內路徑為express.Router()相對路徑，由 LocalPrintService.ts 以 expressApp.use("/api/v1", router) 掛載，完整本機URL為 http://localhost:3003/api/v1 加上檔內路徑，且全部先經 X-API-Key（PRINT_AGENT_API_KEY）驗證；WebSocket（:3004）不是HTTP路由，未列入。行號為撰寫當時的快照，工作樹已有未提交變更的檔案（如orders、guest-orders、app-factory）行號可能漂移。一般GET、DELETE等字串不等於完整contract，務必閱讀其validation/schema。

附錄 B · 資料表與欄位字典

128張Drizzle表的查閱索引；遷移SQL與線上庫仍須分開核對。

Schema快照如何使用

以下是 packages/database/src/schema/ 中literal sqliteTable 宣告的 128張表、1873個欄位。以SQLite欄位名稱對照TypeScript property，可讀出TEXT／INTEGER／REAL等宣告與直接欄位constraint／reference。

這不是線上DB introspection，也不包含control-plane SQL migration所有表、FTS virtual table、SQL-only trigger／CHECK／partial index與所有table-level constraint。INTEGER可能是boolean、cents、毫秒或id，須看欄位的Drizzle mode與validation。此處的flags只列直接出現在column builder的primaryKey／notNull／unique，並非全部約束。

已知Drizzle與migration SQL差異：qr_codes的restaurant_id、created_by原本只存在於Drizzle，baseline SQL與舊軌道migration都沒有（2026-10-05 實測production的qr_codes只有7欄、0筆資料），在缺欄的資料庫上建立／下載QR與QR統計會失敗；migrations_fresh/0037_qr_tenancy_columns.sql補上這兩欄（qr_templates不加欄，以created_by區隔），已於2026-10-05套用到production，既有列的這兩欄為NULL；backup_alerts（triggered_at、resolved_at）、backup_audit_logs（timestamp）、backup_configurations（created_at、updated_at）、backup_records（started_at、completed_at、updated_at）、backup_schedules（last_run_at、next_run_at、created_at、updated_at）、restore_operations（started_at、completed_at）共14個timestamp欄位只存在於SQL，Drizzle未宣告（它們是舊版TEXT時間欄位，Drizzle只對應其整數_ms孿生欄位；備份排程worker的原生SQL仍讀寫TEXT欄位）；重播後的SQL另含輔助表_migration_expected_discount_percentage_bps、_migration_assert_discount_percentage_bps與FTS shadow tables，本字典均未列。

Maintenance and checks

pnpm exec prettier --check docs/user-manuals/system-handbook.html
pnpm exec node scripts/check-system-handbook.cjs

The checks cover duplicate ids, broken anchors, relative source links, chapter coverage, search and print expand / restore. When changing routes or schema, re-check the appendices' static snapshots and source dates; running only the HTML check cannot be taken as business contract verification.
